items.title: Gilmar, l’enfant de Pilimini qui fit danser le Palais de la Kolima
items.description: À Pilimini, dans cette terre du Fouta Djallon réputée pour avoir donné naissance à de grandes figures spirituelles, la musique n’était peut-être pas le destin que sa famille avait imaginé pour Thierno Mamoudou Diallo, plus connu sous le pseudonyme de Gilmar. Et pourtant, c’est bien par la musique que cet enfant de Pilimini allait inscrire son nom dans la mémoire artistique de Labé. Pilimini n’est pas un village comme les autres. Cette terre de Walious, chargée d’histoire et de spiritualité, est notamment associée à la figure de Thierno Aliou M’Bhoubha Diyan, grande figure religieuse et intellectuelle du Fouta. C’est dans cet environnement profondément marqué par la tradition que grandit Gilmar, au sein d’une grande famille de Waliou. Et précisément, cette appartenance familiale allait rendre son choix artistique particulièrement difficile. Quand la passion défie l’interdit Dans sa famille, on ne voulait pas le voir devenir chanteur. Tout semblait avoir été pensé pour l’éloigner de la musique. On raconte même qu’il arrivait que sa chambre soit cadenassée afin de l’empêcher de sortir. Mais on peut enfermer une porte ; on ne peut pas toujours enfermer une vocation. Gilmar trouvait les moyens de s’échapper, de se faufiler, de rejoindre les répétitions et de retrouver cette musique qui semblait déjà avoir choisi sa vie. Là où certains voyaient une désobéissance, lui vivait une passion. Là où sa famille percevait peut-être une rupture avec la tradition, Gilmar semblait avoir découvert une autre manière de porter le nom de sa terre. La musique devint alors son espace de liberté. Et son talent finit par parler plus fort que les interdits. Le « Michael Jackson » de Labé À Labé, Gilmar acquiert rapidement une réputation à part. Sa présence scénique, son énergie et son rapport avec le public lui valent un surnom qui en dit long : le « Michael Jackson » des artistes de Labé. Il n’était pas simplement un chanteur qui montait sur scène pour interpréter des morceaux. Il était un personnage. Une présence. Une voix capable de captiver un public et de transformer une soirée ordinaire en véritable événement. L’engouement qu’il suscitait auprès de ses admirateurs était tel que certains, par affection, admiration ou simplement pour traduire le caractère presque surnaturel de son pouvoir de séduction sur le public, déformaient même son nom de scène. De Gilmar, ils faisaient Djinnarou, terme pular désignant le diable. Le mot pouvait surprendre, voire paraître provocateur. Mais dans la bouche des fans, il traduisait surtout une forme d’admiration populaire : Gilmar était tellement impressionnant sur scène qu’il semblait avoir quelque chose d’irrésistible, presque ensorcelant. Il avait cette capacité rare à tenir un public, à l’entraîner dans son univers et à faire oublier, le temps d’une prestation, tout ce qui se passait autour. Le Palais de la Kolima, son grand théâtre C’est surtout au Palais de la Kolima, haut lieu de la vie culturelle et musicale de Labé, que son nom s’impose. Avec le Kolima Jazz, Gilmar va contribuer à écrire quelques-unes des belles pages de la musique de la cité de Karamoko Alfa. Il n’en est pas un membre fondateur, mais un sociétaire, et cette nuance est importante pour comprendre sa place dans l’histoire de l’orchestre. Le Kolima Jazz avait déjà son histoire, ses pionniers, ses grandes voix et ses musiciens. Gilmar vient enrichir cette grande famille musicale et participer à son rayonnement. Mais l’histoire du Kolima Jazz ne s’est évidemment pas limitée aux murs du Palais de la Kolima. L’orchestre a porté la musique de Labé sur de nombreuses autres scènes de Guinée. Il s’est notamment produit au Palais du Peuple de Conakry et a participé à plusieurs reprises au Festival National des Arts et de la Culture (FENAC), rendez-vous majeur de la célébration du patrimoine artistique guinéen. Son rayonnement a également dépassé les frontières nationales, le Kolima Jazz ayant participé à plusieurs manifestations et festivals au-delà de la Guinée. Ces déplacements ont contribué à faire connaître une autre facette de la création musicale guinéenne et à inscrire l’orchestre de Labé dans le vaste mouvement des musiques africaines. Ainsi, le Palais de la Kolima constituait certes l’un de ses principaux sanctuaires, mais le Kolima Jazz était aussi un orchestre voyageur, capable de porter les sonorités de Labé vers d’autres publics et d’autres horizons. Le Palais de la Kolima, une scène et une école À cette époque, le Palais de la Kolima n’est pas seulement une salle de spectacle. Il est un véritable laboratoire artistique. On y apprend, on y répète, on y forge son identité et, surtout, on y rencontre ceux qui vont marquer l’histoire musicale de Labé. Gilmar y côtoie notamment des doyens et autres sociétaires comme Maître Abdoul Gadiri Diallo, membre fondateur et chef d’orchestre de Kolima Jazz, Tonton Lakis, le regretté doyen Sow Baïlo, Midiaou et Mik Paraya, entre autres. Ensemble, ils offrent au public des moments qui resteront gravés dans les souvenirs des mélomanes. C’est dans cette effervescence que d’autres grandes figures vont également faire leur apparition. Parmi elles, Rizo Bangoura rejoint le Super Kolima Jazz après son passage à Tougué, en 1983. Son arrivée vient encore enrichir le formidable vivier de talents qui gravitent autour de l’orchestre. Et lorsque l’on évoque cette génération, impossible de ne pas mesurer la filiation artistique qui conduira plus tard à l’éclosion d’autres grandes vedettes, notamment Sékouba Fatako, qui viendra, à son tour, « casser la baraque » au Palais de la Kolima. De Pilimini au Palais de la Kolima L’histoire de Gilmar est finalement celle d’un paradoxe fécond. Il est né dans une famille où la tradition religieuse occupait une place majeure. Il est issu de Pilimini, terre de Walious et berceau associé à la mémoire de Thierno Aliou M’Bhoubha Diyan. On aurait pu imaginer pour lui un destin tout tracé, éloigné des lumières de la scène. Mais Gilmar a choisi une autre voie. Il a choisi le chant. Et il l’a choisi avec une telle détermination que les portes fermées, les interdits et même les cadenas n’ont pas suffi à l’arrêter. Son parcours raconte ainsi quelque chose de plus grand que la trajectoire d’un artiste. Il raconte la rencontre entre la tradition et la modernité, la famille et la vocation, la spiritualité et l’expression artistique. À travers Gilmar, c’est aussi une partie de la mémoire musicale de Labé qui ressurgit : celle des soirées du Palais de la Kolima, des orchestres, des sociétaires, des voix puissantes et des musiciens qui ont fait de cette scène un sanctuaire de la musique guinéenne. Mais cette mémoire dépasse les murs du Palais. Elle se prolonge sur les scènes nationales, au Palais du Peuple, dans les festivals comme le FENAC, et jusque sur les scènes extérieures où le Kolima Jazz a porté les couleurs musicales de Labé et de la Guinée. Bien avant que Sékouba Fatako ne fasse trembler les murs du Palais, Gilmar y avait déjà laissé son empreinte. Et dans les souvenirs de ceux qui l’ont vu sur scène, une image demeure : celle de cet enfant de Pilimini qui, malgré les cadenas, avait réussi à ouvrir la porte de son destin. Un enfant devenu artiste. Un artiste devenu phénomène. Et un chanteur dont les admirateurs eux-mêmes, pour traduire l’effet qu’il produisait sur eux, avaient fini par transformer le nom en « Djinnarou ». Gilmar n’a pas seulement choisi la musique. La musique, peut-être, l’avait choisi.

items.title: Les chiffres et les lettres (Par Elhadj Ibrahima THIAM)
items.description: Détrompez-vous : il ne s’agit pas ici de parler de l’émission culte de France 2 qui nous a accompagnés durant notre enfance, à une époque où la culture générale se cherchait dans les livres, les encyclopédies ou ce genre d’instants de télévision, comme nous en avons également connu au Sénégal avec « Génies en herbe » sur la Rts. Rien de cette époque aujourd’hui quelque peu lobotomisée, où ceux qui tiennent le haut du pavé ont pour sphère d’expression TikTok ou Instagram, de véritables instruments d’abrutissement massif. Si bien qu’il est devenu difficile de démêler le vrai du faux. Entre fake news, mésinformation et désinformation, on est abreuvé de flux : une infobésité que l’on a du mal à digérer. Du coup, notre métabolisme en prend un sacré coup. Tenez, à titre d’illustration, cette allégation selon laquelle l’État du Sénégal ne toucherait que… 25 FCfa sur chaque million de Fcfa de pétrole vendu ! Une énormité qui a obligé le ministre de l’Énergie et du Pétrole à se fendre d’un long laïus pour expliquer, à nouveau, encore et encore, l’architecture du partage de la production et des revenus pétroliers. Cette séquence de désinformation est de la même teneur que cette folle rumeur qui avait fait croire, au début de la découverte des champs d’hydrocarbures, que le pétrole sénégalais avait déjà été vendu, poussant certains Sénégalais, niais ou volontairement taquins, à réclamer leurs 400.000 FCfa au frangin de l’ancien Chef de l’État. Dans un tel contexte, lorsque des statistiques officielles, censées provenir de structures institutionnelles, ne sont plus fiables, cela ne fait qu’ajouter au malaise. En effet, il se pose un véritable problème de chiffres au Sénégal. Certes, l’exactitude absolue n’est pas toujours recherchée – une marge d’erreur est tolérée -, mais lorsque, depuis une vingtaine d’années, ce sont les mêmes chiffres qui circulent, alors que, par essence, la dynamique devrait les caractériser, il y a un sérieux souci. Depuis que je suis dans ce métier, au milieu des années 2000, on nous rabâche qu’elle fait vivre 600.000 personnes. Un chiffre qui daterait des années… 1980 Prenez l’exemple de la pêche. Depuis que je suis dans ce métier, au milieu des années 2000, on nous rabâche qu’elle fait vivre 600.000 personnes. Un chiffre qui daterait des années… 1980, m’a-t-on déjà soufflé. Or, depuis au moins 2021, on ne voit plus de rapport annuel qui, au minimum, nous donnerait une idée de la contribution de ce secteur à l’économie. Récemment, le débat sur le dégel d’une catégorie de licences de pêche s’inscrit dans cette même logique de flou qui entoure certaines de nos données statistiques. Le ministère et le Gaipes nagent, allègrement, à rebours. Observez également la polémique annuelle autour des chiffres de la production agricole : entre ce que les pouvoirs publics et certains acteurs avancent, le fossé est si grand qu’il y aurait de quoi y labourer un champ. La Direction de l’analyse, de la prévision et des statistiques agricoles (Dapsa) a beau expliquer ses méthodes de travail et leur fiabilité, ils sont nombreux à ne pas adhérer à ses données. Les résultats de l’audit de l’effectif des agents de la fonction publique en cours – un exercice pourtant réalisé il y a moins de dix ans – vont, eux aussi, raviver la polémique entre l’État et les syndicats sur la fiabilité des données. En ce qui concerne les chiffres macroéconomiques, comme le Pib, le Pnb ou la croissance, on ne sait plus à quel bon chiffre se fier. S’il y a un manque de confiance dans les chiffres, c’est que, très souvent, ils semblent aller dans le sens voulu par l’autorité et sont enrobés de qualificatifs tels que « performance », « une première dans l’histoire », « jamais réalisé ». Des exagérations qui peuvent flatter l’égo, mais qui ne résistent pas à la réalité des faits. Or, en matière de politique publique, des chiffres erronés peuvent tout remettre en cause. De bons chiffres sont des outils d’aide à la décision. Toutefois, tout n’est pas négatif. Il faut saluer les efforts de l’Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (Ansd) qui, régulièrement, s’évertue, à travers les comptes nationaux, à nous donner une idée plus ou moins claire de l’état du pays sur le plan économique et sur bien d’autres points. Il y a aussi le Comité national de l’Initiative pour la transparence dans les industries extractives (Itie), certainement une référence en matière de chiffres, surtout parce que ceux-ci sont actualisés (N-1). D’ailleurs, la semaine dernière, il a publié son rapport portant sur le premier semestre de l’année 2025. Là où d’autres structures publient les leurs à l’improviste ou en N+5. elhadjibrahima.thiam@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Banwa : les fils et filles de la commune de Sanaba reverdissent 1,5 hectares de l’axe Sanaba-Nouna
items.description: Banwa : les fils et filles de la commune de Sanaba reverdissent 1,5 hectares de l'axe Sanaba-Nouna Sanaba,10 août 2026 (AIB)-L'Association pour le développement de la commune de Sanaba (ADCS) a mené ce lundi 10 août 2026, une opération de reboisement sur une superficie de 1,5 hectare, le long de l'axe Sanaba-Nouna. Au total 90 plants composés de baobab, d'anacardier et de moringa ont été mis en terre ainsi que des grains de moringa semés directement sur le site. Avant le démarrage des travaux, des conseils pratiques ont été prodigués aux jeunes par les agents des eaux et forêts, Dieudonné Kouela et Sié Palm sur les techniques appropriées de plantation. Les jeunes se sont ensuite attelés à la mise en terre des plants sur un site déjà clôturé par un grillage en vue de protéger les jeunes pousses contre la divagation des animaux. Le président de l'association Paul Coulibaly a exprimé sa satisfaction au terme de l'activité et a adressé ses remerciements à l'ensemble des jeunes pour leur forte mobilisation. Cette initiative de reboisement vise la restauration du couvert végétal et la sensibilisation des populations à la protection de l'environnement. Agence d'information du Burkina LRS/SO/wis

items.title: Nobody hates you, we want the best for you – Afenyo-Markin tells Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has urged Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi to be more receptive to criticism of the institution. The legislator insisted that the opposition’s concerns are about the Board’s operations and not a personal attack on him. Mr Afenyo-Markin said neither he nor former Deputy Finance Minister Abena Osei Asare harboured any hatred towards Mr Gyamfi despite recent political disagreements over GoldBod. “NPP, nobody hates you. Abena Osei Asare doesn’t hate you. I don’t hate you. We want the best for you,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin’s comments come amid heightened scrutiny of GoldBod and controversy over claims circulating on social media linking a man identified as Dominic Bonsu to Mr Gyamfi’s security detail. The claims have included an allegation that GH¢200 million belonging to GoldBod had been taken by the businessman. Mr Gyamfi has rejected the allegations, describing them as false and part of what he considers a coordinated disinformation campaign against him. Speaking on X Spaces on Sunday, August 9, the GoldBod CEO denied any connection between his bodyguards and gold trading or the alleged loss of state funds. “None of my bodyguards is involved in gold trading, and none of my bodyguards has stolen or taken Gold Board money,” he said. Mr Gyamfi also denied that Mr Bonsu had served as his bodyguard. He said his understanding was that Mr Bonsu was a licensed gold dealer and an executive of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) at the constituency level in the Manso area of the Ashanti Region. “The said Dominic Bonsu, I understand, is even a constituency executive of the NPP somewhere in the Manso area in the Ashanti Region,” Mr Gyamfi said. He also questioned the suggestion that Mr Bonsu had worked as part of his security detail, referring to the physical difference between the two men. GoldBod has separately rejected the allegation of a GH¢200 million loss and the claim that Mr Bonsu was a former bodyguard to the CEO. Mr Afenyo-Markin said Mr Gyamfi should respond to questions about GoldBod on their merits instead of treating criticism as an attack on his character. He also cautioned against allowing political allies or media personalities to attack those who raise questions about the institution. “Some of the people you think are your friends today, that you deploy to attack us merely for questioning certain actions at GoldBod may not be there for you tomorrow,” he said. Speaking on Accra-based Metro TV, the Minority Leader urged Mr Gyamfi to take time to consider the issues raised by the opposition and provide answers rather than respond with attacks. “So, take it easy. When we raise issues, take your time and respond. Don’t come and attack us. Don’t engage others to attack us because we criticise GoldBod,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin also reminded Mr Gyamfi of his conduct while the National Democratic Congress (NDC) was in opposition. “You were very loud when you were in opposition. You raised critical issues. You were the loudest in opposition,” he said. According to the Minority Leader, Mr Gyamfi’s experience in opposition should make him more tolerant of criticism now that he occupies a senior public office. “I am sure you should have a certain level of tolerance to even listen to the issues we raise,” he added. Mr Afenyo-Markin further argued that some of the issues being raised about GoldBod were not simply political accusations made by the opposition. He claimed that some of the concerns had also been raised in reports by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and other institutions he described as credible. “Most of the issues you raise are issues that have been reported by IMF, by institutions that are credible,” he said. The Minority Leader stressed that the opposition’s scrutiny was directed at GoldBod’s activities rather than Mr Gyamfi personally. “We are not after your person. We are after the excesses in the activities at your institution,” he said. He therefore appealed to the GoldBod CEO not to personalise disagreements over the management of the institution. “So please, don’t take it personal. Let’s work together, let’s understand the issues,” Mr Afenyo-Markin said. He also warned Mr Gyamfi that concerns dismissed today could become problematic in the future. “When we raise them, take note, because one day, some of these things may come back and haunt you,” he cautioned. Mr Afenyo-Markin further suggested that individuals who currently defend Mr Gyamfi in the media may not necessarily remain supportive of him in the future. “And maybe a media person that is supporting you today may not be there for you tomorrow,” he added.

items.title: GWL resumes Kpong production after pipeline repairs, consumers to access water in phases
items.description: Ghana Water Ltd (GWL) has resumed water production at the Kpong Treatment Plant following the successful replacement of weak sections of the 21-inch and 42-inch Kpong-Tema transmission pipelines. The maintenance exercise began on Thursday, August 6, 2026, as part of efforts to address weaknesses in the ageing transmission infrastructure serving parts of the Greater Accra and Eastern Regions. GWL said water supply will, however, not return to normal immediately, as transmission lines and reservoirs need to be progressively refilled before operating pressures can be fully restored. “The restoration of supply will be progressive as the transmission lines and reservoirs are filled and operating pressures are gradually rebuilt. Barring unforeseen technical challenges, more consumers are expected to receive water as the system stabilizes,” the company said in a statement issued on Monday, August 10. GWL cautioned consumers against interpreting the resumption of production as an immediate return to continuous water supply. The company’s existing water demand management and rationing programme remains in effect to ensure that available water is distributed equitably while the network stabilises. Customers in affected communities have therefore been advised to continue observing their usual rationing schedules. The company said the transmission network is being closely monitored as supply is progressively restored. Managing Director of Ghana Water Ltd, Adam Mutawakilu, who personally inspected the works at various stages, commended the engineers, contractors, maintenance teams and technical personnel involved in the exercise. He praised them for completing the assignment on schedule despite technical and operational challenges encountered during the maintenance. Mr Mutawakilu particularly acknowledged the Lead and Chief Manager, ATMA Production, Ing. Dr Hadisu Kappus Alhassan, and the General Manager in charge of Operations, Ing. Michael Botse Baidoo, together with their respective teams. “The successful completion of the works demonstrated the value of teamwork, technical expertise, strong coordination and committed leadership in addressing critical infrastructure challenges,” he said. The GWL Managing Director also expressed appreciation to the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) and its Managing Director, Ing. Kwame Kpekpena, for supporting the maintenance exercise. He said ECG’s technical team worked closely with GWL personnel, including through the night, to address critical electrical and operational requirements and facilitate the timely resumption of water production at Kpong. The company also acknowledged support from the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing, the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC), contractors, engineers, field personnel and other stakeholders. GWL said the Kpong-Tema transmission pipelines remain a critical part of the water supply network serving communities in parts of the Greater Accra and Eastern Regions. It urged customers to remain patient as the network is recharged, reservoirs are replenished, and pressures are gradually restored. The company assured consumers that the transmission line would continue to be closely monitored as supply returns progressively.

items.title: Police nab suspected ATM fraudsters in Ekiti, recover 16 cards
items.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Rapid Response Squad (RRS) of the Ekiti State Police Command has arrested three suspected members of a syndicate allegedly specialising in ATM card theft and fraud. The suspects are Timilehin Akinola, 39; Ojo Peter, 46; and Ademola Akinware, 35. The command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Sunday Abutu, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists. According to Abutu, the suspects were arrested following credible intelligence about their presence at the ATM gallery of Wema Bank, Okesa Branch, Ado-Ekiti. He said operatives of the RRS were immediately deployed to the location, adding that the suspects attempted to flee on sighting the police. “Upon sighting the operatives, the suspects, who were riding a TVS motorcycle, attempted to flee the area. The operatives immediately gave them a hot pursuit and successfully intercepted them at the Basiri area of Ado-Ekiti,” the statement said. Abutu said a search conducted on the suspects led to the recovery of 16 ATM cards belonging to different banks and individuals. He added that preliminary investigation indicated that the suspects allegedly specialised in hijacking and swapping ATM cards from unsuspecting members of the public at ATM points within bank premises. The suspects allegedly used the cards to withdraw funds fraudulently from victims’ bank accounts. The Commissioner of Police, Ekiti State Command, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, directed that the investigation be intensified to identify other members of the alleged syndicate and establish the full extent of their activities. The command urged members of the public to remain vigilant while using ATM facilities and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station or the command. The post Police nab suspected ATM fraudsters in Ekiti, recover 16 cards appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Wanted: A ‘Big Push’ for tourism
items.description: When the Minister of Finance stood up to present the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review, I listened closely, the way many of us in this sector do every year. Health got a mention. Education got a mention. Roads got a mention. Agriculture got a mention. Tourism, Culture and the Creative Arts, the sector that keeps our hotels open, our tour guides working, our airlines flying, our artisans selling and our musicians performing, was not mentioned at all. Not one line was set aside for it. This is not a small oversight. I have said for years that tourism is one of the pillars we need if we are serious about moving Ghana’s economy away from depending on just a few exports. When a sector this important is left completely out of a major budget statement, it tells you exactly where that sector sits in the country’s real spending priorities, no matter how good it sounds in speeches. Leaving tourism out of the budget was not an accident. It was a choice. And it is one I believe we must work together to reverse in future budgets. A SECTOR THAT DESERVES MORE SUPPORT I have watched this sector grow over the past ten years, often against the odds. The Year of Return in 2019 turned Ghana into a symbol of homecoming for the African diaspora across the world. Beyond the Return carried that momentum forward. Our heritage sites, beaches, festivals and hospitality businesses still pull in international attention today, but let’s be honest about why: it is mostly private effort, diaspora goodwill and the sheer hard work of operators, not steady government investment, that keeps this going. Imagine what this sector could do if we treated it as the genuine growth engine it is and funded it that way. When the Black Star Experience was launched at the Black Star Square, many of us felt we were finally about to push things a notch higher. OUR NEIGHBOURS ARE NOT STANDING STILL Ghana does not compete for international visitors, diaspora tourists or tourism investment on its own. We are up against our neighbours, and several of them are moving fast. The Gambia recently held a national Tourism Stakeholder Convergence to launch a new, government-approved Marketing, Branding and Investment Promotion Strategy under what it now calls Destination Gambia. It has adopted a Team Gambia approach that puts the private sector at the centre of its international promotion, including a bigger presence at major travel fairs like FITUR. The Gambia is also preparing to host the West African Food Festival this October, using food and cuisine as a fresh way to sell its culture to the world. Senegal, which will host the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, is running a Vision 2050 tourism master plan worth trillions of CFA francs. It is built around one national campaign: Destination Senegal, Land of Teranga. Dakar, Saint-Louis, Saly and Ziguinchor are being developed and marketed together as a single national offer, backed by real government money going into coastal infrastructure. South Africa has gone further still. Its Department of Tourism was given a budget of R2.54 billion for the current financial year, with money deliberately directed to provinces, townships and small towns that had previously been overlooked. It also introduced a new Electronic Travel Authorization to make entry easier for visitors. The results speak for themselves: South Africa welcomed a record 10.5 million international visitors in 2025, and domestic travellers alone generated more than R111 billion in tourism revenue that same year. That is what steady, well-funded political commitment can do. Rwanda tells the same story. Its tourism revenue climbed to $685 million in 2025, up from $647 million the year before, on the back of 1.49 million visitor arrivals. Gorilla trekking alone brought in $248 million, and its conference and events business (MICE) grew to nearly $95 million. Rwanda has built this through years of disciplined, government-backed brand-building, including its well-known Visit Rwanda partnerships that put the country’s name in front of a global audience through sport. It is a small country with a fraction of Ghana’s natural and cultural assets, yet it keeps growing its tourism revenue year after year because it has decided, deliberately, to invest in the brand and protect that investment. Nigeria has entered this race with real seriousness too. Its Ipada initiative, a Yoruba word meaning return, is a structured, multi-year programme to bring people of African descent home, positioning Lagos as a gateway for the diaspora and for global admirers of African culture. This follows the very idea that Ghana pioneered with the Year of Return. Nigeria’s Diaspora Commission and its Tourism Development Authority have since partnered to rebrand the country’s tourism assets and attract fresh investment, and Nigeria has launched a national compendium documenting the tourism and investment potential of all thirty-six of its states. Ghana was the country that first showed the world what diaspora tourism could achieve. We cannot afford to sit back and watch other nations put real money behind the very idea Ghana gave to the whole continent. WHAT GHANA STANDS TO LOSE We do not have the luxury of resting on what we have already achieved while The Gambia, Senegal, South Africa, Rwanda and Nigeria pour real investment into the same market we helped build. Every dollar The Gambia spends sharpening its brand, every rand South Africa puts into provincial tourism infrastructure, every franc Rwanda spends protecting its global visibility, and every naira Nigeria commits to Ipada is chasing the same international traveller, the same diaspora family and the same conference delegate that Ghana also wants to attract. A sector left out of the Mid-Year Budget Review is a sector with no real money to market itself abroad, no real funds to maintain its heritage and cultural sites, no support to train the guides, chefs and hospitality workers who represent Ghana to the world, and no seat at the table when the country decides what matters most. The over reliance on the Tourism Development Fund administered by the Ghana Tourism Authority must give way to major national budget funding similar to what the “big push” is to our roads. A DIRECT REQUEST TO THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE This is a respectful and direct appeal to the Honourable Minister of Finance and to the Ministry as a whole: please take another look at what is allocated to the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts. Give this sector a clear, protected line in the national budget, not scraps from whatever is left over, but a deliberate investment that matches what it has already proven it can do: create jobs, earn foreign exchange, and put young people to work. The people who make up Ghana’s tourism, culture and creative arts community, hoteliers, tour operators, festival organisers, musicians, artisans and heritage custodians, are ready to deliver. What this sector needs now is not another strategy document sitting on a shelf. It needs steady, protected and predictable funding, in line with what our neighbours are already committing. A CALL TO THE SECTOR Here is why this matters, in plain numbers. In 2025 alone, Ghana welcomed over 1.3 million international visitors and earned an estimated $4.34 billion from tourism, one of our largest sources of foreign exchange, alongside gold, cocoa and oil. But look closely, and the warning signs are there: that figure is actually down from $4.82 billion in 2024, not because fewer people came, but because the average visitor is now spending less, about $3,320 in 2025, down from $3,743 the year before. That is what happens when a sector is left to survive on its own momentum instead of being fed with fresh investment, better products and stronger marketing. Meanwhile, domestic travel is doing its part, with almost 1.8 million domestic visits recorded across the country in the same year, proof that Ghanaians themselves believe in what we have. This is the story we should be telling the Ministry of Finance: a sector already worth billions of dollars, already creating jobs in every region, already competing on the same stage as gold and cocoa, but being asked to do it all on it’s own. That is not a funding gap we can afford to ignore. So to everyone working in tourism, hospitality, culture and the creative arts, this is our moment to speak with one voice. Let’s put the jobs, the numbers and the growth potential in front of the Ministry of Finance in terms it cannot brush aside. Ghana’s tourism, culture and creative arts story is too valuable, and too hard-won, to be left out of the very budget that is meant to secure its future. – The author, Akwasi Agyeman, is the Founder and CEO of AFCHAT and former CEO of the Ghana Tourism Authority .

items.title: Mise en garde contre la pêche de la lambouka avant le 15 août
items.description: À l’approche de la mi-août, les regards se tournent vers le démarrage de la saison de pêche à la dorade coryphène (ou lambouka), l’une des espèces saisonnières les plus prisées en Tunisie. Cette période s’accompagne d’appels au respect de la réglementation régissant l’exploitation de cette ressource marine, afin de préserver la durabilité des stocks halieutiques. Conformément à l’arrêté ministériel régissant la saison de pêche à la coryphène pour 2026, l’installation des ghanatis (dispositifs traditionnels de concentration) de poissons est autorisée à partir du 15 juillet, tandis que la saison de pêche proprement dite débute officiellement le 15 août ; toute pêche antérieure à cette date est interdite. À cet égard, l'association Tunsea pour la science participative considère que la mise en vente de coryphènes avant l’ouverture officielle de la saison indique une provenance issue de la pêche illégale. Elle exhorte les consommateurs à s’abstenir de les acheter, soulignant que ce geste contribue à limiter les pratiques de pêche illicites et à protéger les ressources halieutiques. Elle a également été souligné qu’il est impératif de respecter la taille minimale légale de la coryphène (ou lambouka ), fixée à 35 centimètres ; en effet, la pêche ou l’achat de poissons n’atteignant pas cette taille les empêche d’arriver à maturité et de se reproduire, ce qui nuit au renouvellement du stock naturel. La coryphène se distingue par sa croissance rapide : son poids varie entre 400 et 500 grammes en début de saison pour atteindre environ cinq kilogrammes, voire plus, à la fin de celle-ci. Ce poisson prédateur se nourrit de sardines, d’anchois, de maquereaux, de petits poissons, de calmars et de crustacés, jouant ainsi un rôle écologique majeur dans le maintien de l’équilibre de l’écosystème marin. En Tunisie, cette espèce est principalement pêchée à l'aide de ghanatis , des installations marines qui attirent les poissons ayant tendance à se rassembler dans les zones d’ombre ; il s’agit de l’une des plus anciennes techniques de pêche traditionnelle pratiquées dans le pays. La coryphène ( lambouka ) est très prisée des consommateurs tunisiens en raison de ses qualités gustatives et de sa grande valeur nutritionnelle : c’est une source riche en protéines et pauvre en matières grasses, qui contient également des acides gras oméga-3 bénéfiques pour la santé cardiaque et cérébrale. items.title: Niangoloko : Le PDS appelle à une lutte permanente contre les gîtes larvaires pour freiner le paludisme
items.description: Burkina-Comoé-Paludisme-Lutte Niangoloko : Le PDS appelle à une lutte permanente contre les gîtes larvaires pour freiner le paludisme Niangoloko, 10 août 2026 (AIB)- Le président de la Délégation spéciale communale (PDS) de Niangoloko, Ousséni Ouédraogo, a appelé le vendredi 7 août2026, les populations à faire de la destruction des gîtes larvaires et de l’assainissement de leur environnement une responsabilité collective et permanente, à la veille des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV), prévues les 8 et 9 août 2026. « L’assainissement et la destruction des gîtes larvaires » ne doivent pas se limiter aux deux journées consacrées aux JNLAV, mais s’inscrire dans une dynamique communautaire durable visant à maintenir les quartiers et les villages propres et à réduire les conditions favorables à la prolifération des moustiques, a indiqué Ousséni Ouédraogo. M. Ouédraogo s’exprimait vendredi lors d’une rencontre d’information et d’échanges sur les préparatifs des JNLAV 2026 dans la commune de Niangoloko . La rencontre a réuni les autorités administratives et municipales, les directeurs et chefs de services, les leaders coutumiers et religieux, les organisations de la société civile, ainsi que des représentants des associations de femmes et de jeunes et des organisations professionnelles. Selon le PDS, la lutte contre le paludisme ne saurait relever de la seule responsabilité des formations sanitaires. Elle commence dans les concessions, les quartiers, autour des habitations, dans les lieux de rassemblement et partout où des eaux stagnantes peuvent favoriser la prolifération des moustiques vecteurs. « Nous devons faire de l’assainissement et de la destruction des gîtes larvaires une responsabilité collective et permanente », a-t-il insisté, appelant les populations à maintenir leur environnement propre au-delà des activités des JNLAV. Pour le médecin-chef du Centre médical du secteur 06 de Niangoloko, Dr Ismaël Sawadogo, le paludisme demeure « le premier problème de santé publique » au Burkina Faso comme dans la commune. Il a expliqué que la maladie constitue la première cause de consultation et d’hospitalisation dans les formations sanitaires et continue d’occasionner des décès, notamment chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans et les femmes enceintes. Dr Sawadogo a également relevé que la majorité des gîtes larvaires sont d’origine humaine, invitant les populations à changer de comportements. « Ce que l’homme a créé, l’homme peut le détruire », a-t-il soutenu, appelant chacun à contribuer à l’élimination des eaux stagnantes et autres lieux favorables à la reproduction des moustiques. La rencontre a été marquée par une projection sur la lutte anti-vectorielle, présentée et expliquée par le spécialiste en hygiène publique, Boukary Sawadogo, suivie d’une séance d’informations et d’échanges avec les participants. Les Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle 2026 visent notamment à renforcer la prévention du paludisme à travers la destruction des gîtes larvaires et l’assainissement communautaire. Agence d’information du Burkina BBH/no/yos

items.title: Police nab suspected ATM fraudsters in Ekiti, recover 16 cards
items.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Rapid Response Squad (RRS) of the Ekiti State Police Command has arrested three suspected members of a syndicate allegedly specialising in ATM card theft and fraud. The suspects are Timilehin Akinola, 39; Ojo Peter, 46; and Ademola Akinware, 35. The command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Sunday Abutu, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists. According to Abutu, the suspects were arrested following credible intelligence about their presence at the ATM gallery of Wema Bank, Okesa Branch, Ado-Ekiti. He said operatives of the RRS were immediately deployed to the location, adding that the suspects attempted to flee on sighting the police. “Upon sighting the operatives, the suspects, who were riding a TVS motorcycle, attempted to flee the area. The operatives immediately gave them a hot pursuit and successfully intercepted them at the Basiri area of Ado-Ekiti,” the statement said. Abutu said a search conducted on the suspects led to the recovery of 16 ATM cards belonging to different banks and individuals. He added that preliminary investigation indicated that the suspects allegedly specialised in hijacking and swapping ATM cards from unsuspecting members of the public at ATM points within bank premises. The suspects allegedly used the cards to withdraw funds fraudulently from victims’ bank accounts. The Commissioner of Police, Ekiti State Command, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, directed that the investigation be intensified to identify other members of the alleged syndicate and establish the full extent of their activities. The command urged members of the public to remain vigilant while using ATM facilities and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station or the command. items.title: Let’s reconsider 15-month reserves target; rather spend on electricity infrastructure, roads – US-based economist
items.description: The government has been advised to reconsider the 15-month reserves target since it is depriving the nation of domestic capital investments to stimulate economic growth. According to US-based Assistant Professor of Economics at Niagara University, Dennis Nsafoah, a reserve objective closer to the International Monetary Fund’s estimated adequacy level of six months, perhaps with an additional prudential margin, would still provide Ghana with substantial protection against external shocks while freeing significant resources for productive domestic investment. He disclosed this in a paper titled “Why Is Ghana Cutting Capital Expenditure to Pursue Reserves Far Above the IMF’s Adequacy Benchmark?” The lesson from having too few reserves, he argued, should not be that Ghana must accumulate the largest reserve stock possible. “The correct lesson is that Ghana should maintain an adequate buffer while pursuing credible fiscal policy, exchange-rate flexibility and a productive economy capable of continuously generating foreign exchange”, he explained. He also believed that there may be a political attraction to reserves because they provide a highly visible indicator of economic strength, stating that a government can announce that reserves have reached US$20 billion or 10 months of imports much more easily than it can quantify the long-run productivity gains from irrigation, electricity infrastructure or agricultural roads. He added that what is easily measured is not necessarily what produces the highest economic return. Dr. Nsafoah, who is also a member of the Research Committee of Tesah Capital, argued that Ghana does not need to choose between stability and development However, he said that the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP) should not be abandoned. “Its underlying model—building reserves from domestically generated gold rather than borrowed foreign currency—is preferable to the Eurobond-funded reserve accumulation of the past” However, he pointed out that the 15-month target should be reconsidered.

items.title: Le Maroc accueillera la Coupe d’Afrique des moins de 17 ans en 2027
items.description: Le Maroc a été désigné par la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) pour accueillir la Coupe d’Afrique des nations des moins de 17 ans en 2027. La compétition se déroulera entre avril et mai 2027, a annoncé la CAF. Cette désignation confirme une nouvelle fois la place du Maroc parmi les principaux pays hôtes des compétitions africaines. La CAF souligne l’importance des tournois de jeunes dans sa stratégie de développement du football sur le continent. En 2027, le Ghana accueillera la CAN des moins de 20 ans, prévue en février et mars, tandis que l’Égypte organisera la CAN des moins de 23 ans, qui servira de tournoi qualificatif pour les Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028. Une nouvelle compétition féminine à l’étude La CAF envisage également de lancer dès l’année prochaine une nouvelle Coupe d’Afrique des moins de 17 ans féminine, sous réserve que les conditions sportives et organisationnelles soient réunies. Cette compétition permettrait d’offrir une nouvelle plateforme aux jeunes joueuses africaines et s’inscrirait dans la volonté de la CAF de renforcer ses investissements dans le développement du football féminin. Le Maroc sera par ailleurs l’hôte de la Coupe d’Afrique de futsal 2026, programmée du 12 au 21 octobre prochains. La Coupe d’Afrique de beach soccer 2026 se tiendra, elle, au Sénégal en novembre. La CAF a également fait le point sur le projet de Ligue des nations africaine, dont le format a été discuté au sein de son comité exécutif. L’objectif est de proposer davantage de compétitions internationales attractives et de renforcer la valeur sportive et commerciale du football africain. Le calendrier continental se précise Concernant les compétitions interclubs 2026-2027, les tirages des tours préliminaires de la Ligue des champions et de la Coupe de la Confédération ont été effectués. Le premier tour préliminaire se disputera du 4 au 6 septembre 2026, tandis que les matches retour auront lieu du 11 au 13 septembre. Enfin, l’Afrique du Sud accueillera la Supercoupe d’Afrique, prévue le 8 novembre 2026 à Tshwane. Elle opposera les Mamelodi Sundowns, vainqueurs de la Ligue des champions africaine, à l’USM Alger, tenante de la Coupe de la Confédération. À travers ces différentes annonces, la CAF entend mettre en place un calendrier continental plus stable et prévisible, offrant davantage de visibilité aux fédérations, aux clubs, aux joueurs, mais aussi aux diffuseurs, sponsors et supporters. items.title: Army, Air Force, police engage over 100 bandits at Zamfara-Kebbi border
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — A combined force of the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Air Force and Police is currently engaged in a fierce gun battle with more than 100 suspected bandits operating around the Zamfara-Kebbi border. Security sources said the operation involves troops of the Chief of Army Staff Intervention Battalion 3, under 8 Division of the Nigerian Army; the Air Component of Operation Fansan Yamma; and personnel of the Mobile Police Force. The sources said the bandits emerged in large numbers from the Sangeko Gap in Zamfara State and were advancing towards Makuku in Kebbi State when intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance assets detected their movement. According to the sources, the armed group was moving in three separate formations, with the suspected bandits reportedly travelling on motorcycles. The development has heightened security concerns in communities around the affected areas, with some residents reportedly moving to safer locations as security forces intensify efforts to contain the advance. The engagement involves coordinated ground operations by troops and police personnel, supported by air operations by the Air Component of Operation Fansan Yamma. The deployment is aimed at preventing the suspected bandits from gaining access to surrounding communities, disrupting their movement and stopping them from expanding their operations in the area. Residents have been advised to remain vigilant and comply with directives from security authorities while the operation continues. The ongoing engagement highlights the security challenges posed by armed groups operating across parts of the North-West, where security agencies have sustained operations aimed at disrupting criminal networks, rescuing kidnapped victims and restoring normalcy to affected communities. As of the time of filing this report, the security agencies had not released an official casualty figure or confirmed the outcome of the ongoing operation. Further details are expected as the military and other security agencies provide updates. items.title: Ghana earned $4.34 billion from 1.3 million tourist arrivals in 2025 – Tourism Minister
items.description: The Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Dzifa Abla Gomashie, has disclosed that Ghana generated an estimated $4.34 billion from 1.3 million international tourist arrivals in 2025, as the tourism, culture and creative arts sector recorded growth across several key areas. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series on Monday, August 10, the Tourism Minister outlined developments and achievements in the tourism, culture and creative arts sectors since taking office. According to the minister, Ghana recorded 1,303,962 international tourist arrivals in 2025, up from 1,288,804 arrivals recorded in 2024. She said the increase in international arrivals translated into significant revenue for the country, with the sector generating an estimated $4.34 billion in tourism receipts during the year. She also reported growth in domestic tourism, with visits increasing from 1.68 million in 2024 to 1.79 million in 2025, representing a seven per cent increase. The minister also highlighted the performance of Ghana’s major tourist attractions, saying the 10 most visited sites collectively attracted 1,377,588 visitors in 2025. She said the figure represented roughly 27 per cent of all domestic tourism site visits recorded nationwide. The 10 leading attractions were the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, Kakum National Park, Bunso Arboretum Eco Park, Cape Coast Castle, Manhyia Palace, Kumasi Zoo, Accra Zoo, Elmina Castle, Shai Hills Resource Reserve and the Agri-Botanical Garden. Ms Gomashie said that only three of the 10 attractions are directly under the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, while the others are managed through different institutions. The figures, she said, showed the continued importance of Ghana’s tourism sites to both domestic and international tourism and the need for sustained investment in their development and management. The minister also provided an update on efforts to support Ghana’s creative industries. She said a proposed fund for the creative arts was expected to stimulate production, improve the quality of creative content and create jobs, while also strengthening Ghana’s intellectual property position in both local and international markets. “The fund is anticipated to catalyse production activity, improve content quality, create jobs, strengthen Ghana’s intellectual property for both domestic and international markets,” she said. Ms Gomashie disclosed that work was ongoing to finalise the modalities for putting the fund into operation, with the Attorney-General’s Ministry involved in the process. The minister outlined measures being taken to improve the facility and its contribution to the country’s tourism, culture and creative arts industries. She said the ministry had developed a strategic plan for the National Theatre covering the period 2026 to 2030. “We have successfully crafted a strategic plan 2026 to 2030 to guide the running of the National Theatre of Ghana and ensure its optimal contribution to the tourism, culture, and creative arts industry,” she said. According to the minister, the strategic plan was launched in March 2026 and is intended to provide a clear direction for the management and development of the facility. She also disclosed that the ministry had negotiated support from a German theatre group, resulting in the donation of a 40-foot container filled with lighting and sound equipment for the National Theatre.

items.title: Wike denies lobbying for APC campaign council DG
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has debunked reports in some sections of the media suggesting that he was lobbying to be made Director General of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council PCC. Reacting through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the monister described the report as false, saying he did not at any time discuss the leadership or even membership of the Presidential Campaign Council with anyone. A national newspaper (not Vanguard) had on Monday listed the FCT minister among top party chieftains and government officials lobbying or being mentioned for the position of APC Presidential Campaign Council DG. Wike, who reiterated his unflinching support for the reelection of President Bola Tinubu, said he does not need to be the DG or even a member of the President’s Campaign Council to ensure that the President wins massively in Rivers State and the FCT. “I am outside Nigeria, resting and relaxing after spending over 30 days, commissioning projects, flagging off new ones and inspecting ongoing ones, especially those scheduled for commissioning in December and January, next year. “When I return, our focus will be the continuous delivery of our mandate in line with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda and to further enhance his electoral fortune in Rivers State and the FCT. “Therefore, I do not need to be the DG or even member of the Presidential Campaign Council of Mr President’s political party to contribute my quota by ensuring that he wins handsomely in Rivers State and the FCT,” Wike who is now the leader of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party PDP said. The post Wike denies lobbying for APC campaign council DG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 3rd phase of AJK elections: Polling concludes in Poonch Division's Bagh, Haveli districts
items.description: Polling in four constituencies of Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts concluded on Monday as part of the third phase of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections. Elections are being held across AJK in phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Citing law and order concerns, the Election Commission had decided to postpone polling in Bagh and Sudhnoti districts that was originally set for today. On Monday, polling began at 8am and continued until 5pm in four Poonch constituencies. The PPP, which has accused the PML-N of rigging in the previous phases, continued to make similar allegations on Monday as well. In response, PML-N leaders said the PPP had no evidence for its claims, and reiterated their confidence to form the government in AJK based on the seats it has already secured so far. The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. On the other hand, the PPP has only won 10 constituencies so far. The third phase of the AJK elections was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21. Government officials had anticipated clashes in some areas today, while the Election Commission had classified most of the 803 polling stations in the four constituencies as either sensitive or highly sensitive. “Apart from the regular police of both districts, we have dispatched an additional 10,300 troops to maintain law and order and provide a fear-free atmosphere to voters,” Election Commission Secretary Raja Mohammad Shakeel told Dawn earlier Malpractice, rigging allegations Polling in previous phases of the elections was marred by allegations of rigging , scuffles and violence, with the PPP and the PML-N — the main contenders in AJK but allies in the Centre — engaging in a war of words. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging and electoral malpractices in the previous phases. It continued to allege rigging in Haveli and Bagh as well. In a series of posts on X, the PPP shared complaints it said it had filed to the Election Commission. In one of the complaints, the PPP alleged that roads leading to the Banni Marasira area had been blocked, where PML-N supporters were illegally stamping ballot papers at 12 polling stations in the LA-15 constituency. “The commission is requested to consider the two acts together rather than separately, because the second is made possible by the first,” the party said, adding that officials, voters, polling agents and party workers were unable to reach the polling stations “to see what is being done inside”. The party also claimed delays in polling at LA-15’s polling station no.87 in Thub. It also alleged that polling at stations no.143 and 144 in Hatala Pader did not commence on time due to the non-arrival of polling staff. The PPP also alleged that its polling agent was “forcibly removed” from LA-15’s station no.158 in Makhdoom Kot. Similarly, PPP’s agents had also been removed from polling stations no.8-14 in Bani Maldhara and PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers at those stations, the party alleged. At around 12:45, the party claimed on X that workers of Jamaat-i-Islami had gathered to “capture” 26 polling stations in the constituency — nos.31-38, nos.70-79 and nos.180-186. It said the police had initially arrived but then withdrew. “The stations are, therefore, unguarded at this moment, with an organised body assembled against them.” It urged the Election Commission to determine on whose orders police had withdrawn and direct the law enforcers to return to the station. The PPP also posted a blurry video, which it said was of PML-N workers “attacking” the polling station set up at the Boys Middle School in LA-15 Central Bagh. Regarding LA-16, the party claimed that its polling agents were not being allowed inside stations no.119 and 120 while PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers inside the stations in the agents’ absence. The PPP further alleged delays in polling at stations no.61 and 141 of the constituency. It made similar allegations regarding polling stations no.109 and 110 in LA-16 Bagh-III Sharqi. Moreover, the party accused “armed individuals associated with the PML-N” of opening fire at polling station no.179, Kot Chinalla in the constituency and disrupting the election process. “The polling agents of the PPP have been removed from the station. It is further alleged that ballot papers are being stamped lawfully,” the PPP added. In LA-17, the party alleged that its agents had been “forced out” from the polling station in Mullah Basti, Kahuta City by PML-N workers. PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman expressed reservations after reports of rigging and malpractices emerged, saying that preventing polling agents from entering polling stations in LA-16 raised “serious questions” about the transparency of the election process. In a statement, she demanded that an explanation be sought from the presiding officers of stations nos.119 and 120 on the matter. The senator also called for the Election Commission to take notice of the reports of PPP’s polling agent being removed from station no.158 in LA-15. Rehman further demanded alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortage of polling staff and material, calling on the authorities to ensure that free and transparent elections were held at all polling stations without any disruption. PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari also accused the PML-N of continuing rigging in the third phase of the elections. He highlighted that his party was regularly informing the Election Commission about the alleged rigging via phone. But, “the chief election commissioner and the election commission secretary’s reply to all of our complaints has been that nothing has happened and everything is good,” he claimed. When Dawn approached the Election Commission regarding Bokhari’s claim, Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel said any complaint that he or the chief election commissioner received was being attended and responded to, and the Quick Response Force (QRF) was also moved over it. ‘AJK’s people have supported PML-N’ Responding to PPP’s allegations, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said the rival party had not provided any proof for its claims. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad flanked by Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, Sanaullah denied that a comparatively high turnout could be considered proof of rigging. The PML-N leader explained that a strong family and tribe system in AJK prompted people to show up for their relatives. “Our opposing candidate Chaudhry Yasin was complaining yesterday that in his opposing candidate’s union council (UC), 80pc votes were cast, whereas in his own UC, 96pc votes were cast,” Sanaullah claimed. Sanaullah asserted that balloting had gone fairly smoothly in Bagh and Haveli today. He, however, detailed a few reported incidents. In Haveli, people tried to snatch documents from the polling agents in one station, but the Quick Response Force (QRF) promptly responded and resolved the situation without incident, according to Sanaullah. In Bagh, some people, whom Sanaullah claimed were PPP workers, tried to halt polling at three stations. QRF responded there as well and resumed polling, the minister added. Meanwhile, Muqam urged PPP to review the number of people attending their rallies instead of accusing others of rigging, insisting that PPP lacked support from the people of AJK. “AJK’s people have supported PML-N,” Muqam asserted. Disputing PPP’s recent stance that it was against phased elections, Muqam said the party had mentioned no reservations when the election schedule was first announced . Sanaullah also backed Muqam, saying that PPP had not raised concerns when the Election Commission had originally sought consent from all parties for phased elections. He further claimed that upon PPP’s insistence, the electoral watchdog had scheduled voting on the 12 refugee seats in the second phase of the elections. Sanaullah contended that PPP did not want election results from the refugee seats in the rest of Pakistan to impact its numbers in AJK polls since PPP had not even canvassed in those places. Speaking about the recent unrest in the region, Sanaullah expressed hope that the protests would end once the third phase of elections concludes, as protesters had “only aimed to stop elections”. The new AJK government, which he said PML-N would form with a two-thirds majority, will respond to the protesters’ “valid demands”, the PML-N leader added. However, he also warned that those who “took up arms and instigated the people of AJK, while acting on the directions of the enemy… will have to face the law and answer for their crimes”. In response to a reporter’s question about PPP’s claim that PML-N only had numbered days of rule in the Centre, Sanaullah expressed hope that after the AJK elections, PPP would “open-heartedly” congratulate PML-N. Meanwhile, PML-N’s AJK chapter secretary general Tariq Farooq — who also emerged as the winner in LA-7 recently — said allegations of “rigging, violence, coercion, or fake voting” emerging from the constituency of Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore were a “serious question of constitutional governance”. “This is no longer merely an electoral dispute. It becomes a serious question of constitutional governance, democratic values, and the sanctity of the people’s vote,” Farooq wrote on X. “I find it difficult to believe that the prime minister of Azad Jammu & Kashmir could consider himself above the Constitution, the law, and basic ethical obligations merely to secure his own election,” he said, without providing further details. The PML-N candidate asserted that “public mandate must be secured through a free, fair and transparent election, not through power, influence or state authority”. Rathore, two ex-AJK PMs face crucial electoral test In Monday’s polls, AJK PM Rathore, who is from the PPP, and two of his predecessors — Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan — face a battle for political survival as voters head to the polls. Around 238,664 men and 221,707 women are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations comprising 1,254 polling booths. A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with LA-14 (Dhirkot) attracting the highest number of candidates at 30 and LA-17 (Haveli) the lowest at nine. In LA-17, Rathore is facing PML-N candidate Mohsin Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, a member of the AJK Council. Rathore and Saeed had been political allies and, under an agreement, had agreed to contest the seat alternately. However, after becoming prime minister, Rathore asked Saeed to step aside in his favour, a request he did not accept, turning the former allies into rivals. Aziz, whose father Chaudhry Mohammad Aziz had won the seat at least three times, draws support from the sizeable Gujjar community. His recent large election rally in Forward Kahuta reportedly surprised his rivals and underscored the strength of his campaign. Saeed, meanwhile, is believed to enjoy the backing of a sizeable section of the Kashmiri community, as well as an alliance of several smaller clans. Rathore, however, remains confident of retaining the seat, citing the performance of his government during his relatively brief tenure as prime minister. The constituency has also witnessed allegations of electoral irregularities on social media, with reports claiming that two presiding officers had been caught manipulating results in favour of Rathore. Shakeel dismissed the allegations but at the same time confirmed that complaints had been received against the two officials and that they had subsequently been relieved of election duties. In LA-15 (Wasti Bagh), ex-PM Ilyas is facing PML-N candidate and former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, PPP nominee and sitting minister Sardar Ziaul Qamar, and Jamaat-i-Islami candidate retired Brig Dr Mohammad Khan, a respected educationist. Ilyas, who secured a little over 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum in the second phase of the elections, had initially announced a boycott of the third phase. He subsequently reversed the decision and resumed campaigning, claiming that his victory would enable the constituency to “secure either the presidency or prime ministership.” Ilyas and Qamar belong to the same Madiyal tribe, while Brig Khan belongs to the Narma clan and enjoys the support of former JI chief Abdul Rashid Turabi and former adviser Raja Yasin Khan. Minhas has the advantage of belonging to the PML-N, which is poised to form the next government after emerging as the largest party in the elections held so far. His campaign has also stressed the argument that voters should elect a candidate from the party that is set to occupy the government benches rather than send their representative to the opposition. In LA-16 (Sharqi Bagh), former ministers Sardar Mir Akbar and Sardar Qamar Zaman are the principal contenders, representing the PML-N and PPP, respectively. The fourth contest, LA-14 (Dhirkot), has drawn particular attention because of the challenge faced by Sardar Attique, head of the once-dominant Muslim Conference (MC). Attique is reportedly facing a strong challenge from Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the relatively new Awam Dast-o-Bazu Party. A contractor and philanthropist, Abbasi is said to have spent millions of rupees from his own resources on public welfare projects in the constituency, helping him build a sizeable personal following. Attique, who has represented the constituency successively since 2006, when he first became prime minister, faces an additional challenge in that Abbasi also belongs to the same tribe. Among nearly two dozen other candidates are PML-N’s nominee Raja Faisal Azad and PPP candidate Raja Mubashar Ejaz. While the main contest is seen as being between Attique and Abbasi, the PML-N and PPP nominees are expected to vie for the second runner-up position. Additional reporting by Tariq Naqash

items.title: Une aide-ménagère grièvement brûlée à l’eau bouillante aux Parcelles Assainies
items.description: Le Commissariat d'arrondissement de Golf Sud a annoncé l'interpellation d'un individu, le 7 août 2026, pour des faits de blessures volontaires et de mise en danger de la vie d'autrui. L'information a été révélée ce 10 aout 2026 via un communiqué de la Police. Les faits se sont déroulés vers 14 heures à l'Unité 03 des Parcelles Assainies. Une jeune aide-ménagère aurait été victime de graves violences au domicile de son employeuse. D'après le communiqué policier, la victime aurait été ébouillantée à la suite d'une altercation dont les circonstances restent encore à établir. Ce sont des riverains qui ont réagi les premiers, transportant la jeune fille au poste de santé de l'Unité 04 pour qu'elle reçoive des soins d'urgence. Face à la gravité de ses blessures, les policiers ont dû faire appel aux sapeurs-pompiers, qui ont assuré son évacuation vers l'Hôpital Principal de Dakar. La mise en cause a depuis été placée en garde à vue, et l'enquête se poursuit pour « faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire », selon les termes du communiqué. O.B.N

items.title: GNACOPS refuses to submit BECE evidence directly to WAEC, demands independent prob
items.description: The Executive Director of the Ghana National Council of Private Schools (GNACOPS), Obenfo Nana Kwasi Gyetuah, says private schools will not submit evidence of alleged discrepancies in the 2026 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) results directly to the West African Examinations Council (WAEC). He explained that the evidence would instead be presented to an independent body if one is established to investigate the concerns raised by private schools. Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem ,on August 10, Obenfo Gyetuah rejected calls for private schools to provide their evidence directly to WAEC, arguing that the examination body is itself at the centre of the concerns. “Nobody has said we don’t have basis or evidence. We’re saying we will not give it to WAEC. Why should we give it to WAEC?” he asked. He said the private schools would release the evidence only as part of an independent investigation, where the process would be separate from WAEC. “So nobody should be there demanding evidence because it is not in the media that we will present those evidence,” he said. “That is why we’re requesting for the independent body to be established for whatever discussion there is to be held. If we know we are investigating the work of WAEC, then we bring the evidence,” he added. His comments follow concerns raised by GNACOPS and some private schools over the 2026 BECE results, with the group alleging discrepancies in the performance of candidates from private schools. GNACOPS has petitioned the Ministry of Education over the matter and called for an independent investigation to establish whether the concerns raised are justified. The development has triggered a wider debate, with some education stakeholders urging private schools to provide concrete evidence to support their allegations. The Head of Public Affairs at WAEC, John Kapi, has also rejected suggestions that the Council deliberately targeted private schools, insisting that the allegations must be supported by evidence. Mr Kapi said WAEC had no reason to target private schools and noted that some staff of the Council also have children attending private schools. However, Obenfo Gyetuah questioned why WAEC was demanding evidence while, according to him, the Council had not made available the examination scripts needed to independently assess the concerns. “Mr Kapi is saying he is embarking on an assessment, and he hasn’t seen any script from the private schools. Why are they also refusing to release the scripts of the students?” he asked. He said the issue should be handled carefully by all sides rather than turning it into a public confrontation. “So let’s all be quiet, because how do you expect me to bring the evidence to the same body we have an issue with?” he said. GNACOPS maintains that an independent investigation would provide a more credible platform for examining the alleged discrepancies and determining whether there were any irregularities in the 2026 BECE results. The group is therefore insisting that any evidence supporting its concerns should be presented to an independent body rather than to WAEC itself.

items.title: Army, police rescue kidnapped victim in Edo, recover ransom
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – PERSONNEL of 4 Brigade Nigerian Army in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, have rescued a kidnapped victim identified as Lucky Egbiki during a coordinated operation in Ubiaja, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State. The 50 years old Egbiki was kidnapped at his farm in Ubiaja, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State. A statement on Sunday by the Brigade’s Assistant Director Army Public Relations, Captain Kennedy Anyanwu rescue operation was conducted “at about 1800 hours on 6 August 2026 by troops, in conjunction with personnel of the Nigeria Police. The security forces exploited ransom negotiations to lure the kidnappers to a predetermined location at Onogholo, within Esan South East Local Government Area, where they engaged the criminal elements.” He said during the encounter, one of the kidnappers who arrived at the location to collect the ransom was neutralized by the troops, forcing the other members of the gang to abandon the victim and flee into the surrounding forest, with some believed to have sustained gunshot wounds. He said the troops subsequently rescued the victim unhurt and recovered the sum of ₦1.5 million intended as ransom payment. “The rescued victim was handed over to his family after preliminary debriefing and medical assessment, and was confirmed to be in stable condition.” Anyanwu said the successful operation further demonstrated the Nigerian Army’s operational readiness, intelligence-driven approach and unwavering commitment to combating kidnapping and other forms of violent crime in Edo State and “It also underscores the importance of inter-agency collaboration in enhancing the effectiveness of security operations. “The people of Edo State are therefore encouraged to continue providing timely, credible and actionable information to security agencies, as such support remains vital to sustaining operational successes and enhancing security across the state.” The Commander, 4 Brigade Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ahmed Balogun, commended the troops for their proactiveness, courage and professionalism displayed during the operation and reassured the people of Edo State that the Brigade would continue to apply sustained pressure on kidnappers and other criminal elements operating within its area of responsibility. “The Commander further affirmed that troops would sustain aggressive and intelligence-led operations aimed at denying criminal elements safe havens, protecting lives and property, and creating a secure environment for farming and other legitimate economic activities across Edo State.” The post Army, police rescue kidnapped victim in Edo, recover ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Video: ‘My daughter needs treatment’ – Nigerian US army woman begs Trump over visa denial
items.description: A Nigerian woman serving in the United States Army has appealed to President Donald Trump to intervene in a visa dispute preventing her 10-year-old daughter from joining her in the US. The woman said her daughter is critically ill and requires urgent medical attention that she believes is difficult to access in Nigeria. She made the appeal in a video posted on TikTok, saying she had been separated from her daughter for about 10 years and feared she could lose her before they have the opportunity to reunite. She said she had taken an oath to serve the United States and remained compliant with the country’s laws, but was now seeking Trump’s intervention as a mother desperate to save her child. “Please do not scroll. I’m at the verge of losing my daughter. They said social media is powerful, and this is my last resort.” According to the woman, her daughter had completed the necessary immigration process but remained unable to travel to the US because of current visa restrictions. She said the child became critically ill while the family waited for the immigration process to be completed, increasing her concern over the girl’s access to adequate medical care. “I’m not just speaking as a soldier; I’m speaking as a mother whose heart is gradually breaking. I have been separated from my daughter for the past 10 years, and she remains in Nigeria,” she said. “Every day that passes by increases my fear that I might lose her before having the chance to hold her again and reunite with her.” The US Army member acknowledged the importance of immigration laws and national security but urged the government to consider her circumstances on humanitarian grounds. “My plea now is not about politics but a humanitarian one, a compassionate one that you should review carefully and consider. I’m simply asking that there should be an exception for me and for people that fall into this category,” she said. She also questioned why she should remain in the US, where she said her daughter could have access to better healthcare, while the child remains critically ill in Nigeria. “How can I be in a country that has quality healthcare and let my daughter die?” she asked. She disclosed that she had contacted her commander and US Senator Amy Klobuchar for help, saying the senator attempted to intervene but was informed that the immigration process was proceeding as expected. “I’ve reached out to my commander and Senator Amy Klobuchar. She tried her best, and they told her everything is going as planned. But your visa process and policies are keeping my children from reuniting with me,” she said. She further said she could not return to Nigeria because of security concerns, arguing that her children should not be viewed as a threat to the United States. “My kids are barely minors that can’t pose a threat and are not coming here to be criminals,” she said. She subsequently appealed to social media users to share the video and tag Trump, saying she had turned to social media after exhausting other options. “I never thought a day would come that I would be facing the camera and pleading. Dear Mr President, please help me reunite with my daughter,” she said. Vanguard News The post Video: ‘My daughter needs treatment’ – Nigerian US army woman begs Trump over visa denial appeared first on Vanguard News .
