items.title: Onoh tackles SA envoy over xenophobia denial, demands protection for Nigerians
items.description: By Dennis Agbo ABUJA — Former member of the Enugu State House of Assembly and former Southeast spokesman for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Chief Okey Onoh, has criticised the South African Consul-General to Nigeria, Prof. Bobby Moroe, over his denial of xenophobia in South Africa. Moroe, in a recent interview, had assured Nigerians that South Africa remained safe for tourists, business travellers and other visitors, insisting that “there’s no xenophobia in South Africa” when asked about reported attacks on foreigners. Reacting in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja, Onoh disagreed with the envoy, arguing that the denial did not reflect the experiences of African migrants in South Africa. He alleged that xenophobic and anti-immigrant sentiments remained a serious concern in parts of the country, citing reported attacks on foreign nationals and activities of groups he identified as Operation Dudula and other anti-immigrant organisations. According to Onoh, the activities of such groups had created fear among African migrants and affected their businesses and livelihoods. He also cited reports by human rights organisations and research bodies which, he said, had documented anti-immigrant sentiments and incidents involving attacks or discrimination against migrants. Onoh argued that South Africa’s domestic economic and security challenges should not be blamed on African migrants, alleging that foreigners had sometimes been used as scapegoats for wider social and economic problems. He called on the South African government to do more to protect foreign nationals and prosecute those responsible for attacks and discrimination against migrants. Onoh also criticised what he described as the silence of some South African officials over reported attacks against African migrants, saying the country should uphold the principles of African solidarity that characterised the struggle against apartheid. He recalled the support provided by African countries, including Nigeria, during the anti-apartheid struggle, arguing that the continent’s solidarity should be reciprocated through the protection of African nationals living and doing business in South Africa. The former lawmaker further called for what he described as a coordinated continental response to attacks against African migrants in South Africa. He argued that African countries should reconsider the economic and diplomatic benefits extended to South Africa if the safety and rights of their citizens could not be guaranteed. Onoh said Nigeria should prioritise the safety and dignity of its citizens, while urging the South African authorities to address concerns surrounding xenophobic violence and discrimination. Concluding his statement, Onoh said: “Keep your South Africa, while we keep our Nigeria.” He maintained that Nigerians should feel safe and protected in their own country and urged the South African government to take concrete measures to protect African migrants and strengthen peaceful relations among African nations. The post Onoh tackles SA envoy over xenophobia denial, demands protection for Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sourou/IPO : Le président de la cellule provinciale exhorte les appelés à s’identifier aux personnes qui incarnent les valeurs d’intégrité
items.description: BURKINA–SOUROU–IPO–CEREMONIE- LANCEMENT Sourou/IPO : Le président de la cellule provinciale exhorte les appelés à s'identifier aux personnes qui incarnent les valeurs d'intégrité Tougan, 28 juil. 2026 (AIB) – La deuxième édition de l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) a été officiellement lancée, mardi à Tougan, au cours d'une cérémonie présidée par le Haut-Commissaire de la province du Sourou, Désiré Badolo, président de la cellule provinciale de l'IPO. À cette occasion, il a exhorté les appelés à être des modèles dans la société et à s'identifier aux personnes qui incarnent les valeurs d'intégrité. La cérémonie de lancement a été principalement marquée par la diffusion du message du Président du Faso à l'endroit des nouveaux bacheliers appelés à effectuer leur immersion patriotique. À cette occasion, Djata Drabo, appelée de l'édition 2025, a livré, au nom de l'ensemble des appelés de la première édition du Sourou, un message de partage d'expérience et de motivation à l'endroit des nouveaux bacheliers. « Cette immersion n'est pas une punition, mais une forge où le feu de la discipline, le marteau de l'exigence et l'enclume de la rigueur façonneront l'homme et la femme que vous êtes appelés à devenir », a-t-elle déclaré. Le Haut-Commissaire de la province du Sourou, par ailleurs président de la cellule provinciale de l'IPO, Désiré Badolo, a, pour sa part, exhorté les appelés à devenir des modèles au sein de la société. « Aujourd'hui s'ouvre une nouvelle vie. L'immersion est une école de vie. À travers cette école, identifiez-vous davantage à ceux qui incarnent les valeurs qu'à ceux qui font des pieds et des mains pour être riches dans la société », a-t-il lancé. Le président de la cellule provinciale de l'IPO a félicité les nouveaux bacheliers, salué l'engagement de l'ensemble des acteurs mobilisés pour la réussite de cette deuxième édition et souhaité à tous une excellente session d'immersion patriotique. items.title: Abia new CP, Afolabi assumes duty, vows zero tolerance for misconduct
items.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State has a new Commissioner of Police, Mr Wilfred Afolabi, who assumed duty on Monday with a pledge to strengthen intelligence-led policing, deepen community partnership and enforce discipline within the rank and file. CP Afolabi, who becomes the 35th Commissioner of Police in Abia, succeeds AIG Danladi Isa, who has been promoted and redeployed to the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) Annex, Kaduna. The new CP, who spoke to journalists shortly after assuming office, said his administration would focus on strengthening existing security structures and re-engineering the state’s intelligence network to enhance crime prevention. “Because of my intelligence background, intelligence is really going to be given much priority. We are going to make sure that intelligence structures are re-engineered and the intelligence network enhanced,” he said. The new CP said his administration would replicate the agenda of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, in Abia, particularly the objective of building a police force that discharges its responsibilities with professionalism and dignity. He disclosed that his first major engagement after assuming duty would be with the intelligence department, underscoring the importance he attaches to intelligence gathering. The new CP also promised to take community policing to a new level through regular engagement with stakeholders, including traditional rulers, youth and religious leaders, hoteliers, pharmacists and school proprietors. According to him, such engagement would create a “two-way traffic” through which residents could communicate their security concerns to the police while also providing useful information for crime prevention. “When there is mutual trust, there will be free flow of information. They will feel free to share information with us,” he said. Vows to prepare Abia police for 2027 polls As the 2027 general elections draw closer, Afolabi said his administration would embark on extensive capacity building for officers, including training on electoral laws, human rights, emotional intelligence, crime mapping and investigation. He said officers would also undergo physical and operational preparedness exercises ahead of the elections. “We need to make our officers undertake what I call combat courses,” he said. The CP further promised to review existing crime prevention strategies and introduce new approaches where necessary, while ensuring greater professionalism and uniformity in the handling of police case files. ‘We won’t spare deviant officers’ Afolabi also came down hard on police personnel who deliberately abuse their powers, warning that officers who commit serious offences would face the full weight of disciplinary procedures. He said his administration would combine mentoring and capacity building with firm disciplinary measures. “If, after investing millions in training you, you still decide to become a deviant, be rest assured that we are not going to treat your matter with kid gloves,” he warned. He gave an instance of any officer who unjustifiably shoots a motorist, saying such conduct would not be excused through intervention by traditional rulers or religious leaders. “You cannot go and shoot a motorist along the highway now for no justifiable reason and expect that you will bring your king or your religious leader to come and beg me. I will not forgive you,” he said. However, Afolabi said not every breach of duty would automatically attract dismissal, stressing that officers whose shortcomings arose from inadequate professional training would be mentored and retrained. To prioritize welfare of officers The new CP also listed police welfare among his priorities, arguing that officers who are properly catered for would be more motivated to perform their duties effectively. “When our officers are taken care of and catered for, you get the best out of them,” he said. He also pledged to maintain discipline within the command, declaring that his personal discipline would be reflected in the standards expected of officers under him. Promises media-friendly administration Afolabi also assured journalists of a cordial working relationship, describing the media as critical partners in crime prevention, public enlightenment and confidence-building between the police and the public. He promised regular interaction with the media in Abia, stressing that journalists should report both the successes and shortcomings of the police. “I’m not saying if I’m not doing well, you should keep quiet,” he said. Afolabi said he respected journalists and regarded them as partners in the war against crime. Meanwhile , a statement issued later by the Police Public Relations Officer PPRO, Maureen Chinaka, described CP Afolabi as a seasoned police officer with over three decades of service, who was enlisted as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police in 1992 and holds degrees in Botany and Peace and Security Studies. It said Afolabi had served in several strategic command positions, including Commissioner of Police in Ondo State, CP Admin, Training and Development at Force Headquarters, and senior operational and investigative roles in Delta, Katsina, Bayelsa, Anambra, Imo and Abuja. “Afolabi also has extensive international policing experience, having served with the African Union Mission in Sudan and the United Nations Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he was involved in police reforms, training and peacekeeping operations. “His professional training includes strategic and tactical leadership, internal security, low-intensity conflict and peacekeeping negotiation”, the statement said. The post Abia new CP, Afolabi assumes duty, vows zero tolerance for misconduct appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 22% gap persists between urban and rural access to basic drinking water – Local Gov’t Ministry
items.description: Access to basic drinking water services in Ghana stands at 96.4% in urban areas compared with 74.4% in rural communities , exposing a 22-percentage-point gap in access, according to data cited by the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs. The figures highlight persistent disparities in access to essential water services despite progress at the national level. According to the 2021 Population and Housing Census data referenced by the Ministry, 87.7% of households nationwide have access to basic drinking water services , while 92% use improved sources of drinking water. However, the urban-rural divide remains significant, with rural households lagging considerably behind their urban counterparts. The Ministry says the disparity underscores the need for continued investment in water infrastructure and stronger local-level interventions, particularly in underserved communities. The figures were highlighted as Ghana joined other African countries to commemorate the 2026 African Day for Decentralisation and Local Development on Monday, August 10. This year’s observance is themed “Empowered Local Governments for Sustainable Water and Sanitation: Advancing Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Cities and Territories towards Agenda 2063.” The Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs said empowering Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) is critical to improving access to essential services, including water and sanitation. It said government is working to strengthen local governments through improved institutional capacity, sustainable financing arrangements and partnerships involving Regional Coordinating Councils, MMDAs, Ghana Water Limited and the Community Water and Sanitation Agency. Development partners, civil society organisations, traditional authorities and religious institutions are also expected to play a role in addressing water and sanitation challenges. The Ministry said traditional and religious leaders are particularly important in mobilising communities, promoting responsible water use and supporting local initiatives aimed at improving sanitation and environmental management. It said reducing the gap between urban and rural communities would require sustained investment and stronger local institutions capable of responding to the specific needs of their communities. The government therefore urged stakeholders to renew their commitment to decentralised governance and support local authorities to improve service delivery as Ghana works towards the Sustainable Development Goals and the African Union’s Agenda 2063.

items.title: Late night terrorist attack on Upper Swat police post foiled: DPO
items.description: SWAT/ BANNU: A terrorist attack on the Chatkekal police post near Jarogo Waterfall in Upper Swat was foiled after police personnel mounted a strong counterattack late on Sunday night, District Police Officer (DPO) Mushtaq Ahmad said. According to police, more than 12 terrorists surrounded the post and opened fire from all sides. The police personnel deployed at the post immediately retaliated with effective gunfire, forcing the attackers to retreat and flee the area. Initial reports suggest that two terrorists were injured in the exchange of fire. Security personnel have intensified surveillance in the area, while further details are being ascertained. The DPO praised the personnel deployed at the post for their prompt response and bravery, saying Swat police remained at the forefront of the fight against terrorism. “Such cowardly attacks cannot demoralise Swat Police. Our personnel know how to respond effectively to terrorist attacks,” he said. The attack came a week after a suicide bombing near the Kabal Police Station in Swat district claimed 17 lives , including seven policemen. The blast took place while a protest against lawlessness was under way at the adjoining Kabal Chowk. On Friday, thousands of people from across Swat district gathered at Nishat Chowk in Mingora to condemn the suicide bombing and to reaffirm their commitment to peace in the valley. Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS), security personnel deaths in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed. Constable martyred, terrorist killed Separately, a cop was martyred in Bannu when unidentified attackers, suspected to be terrorists, opened fire on him near the Hamza Tablighi Markaz located along the Bannu-Miranshah Road in the Baka Khel area, police said. Police said Constable Anwarullah Khan, who was deployed at the Baka Khel police station, died at the scene while the attackers fled. The officials added that a large contingent of police reached the site after receiving information about the attack, cordoned off the area and launched a search for the assailants. They said evidence from the crime scene was being collected and efforts were underway to identify and arrest those involved in the attack. Meanwhile, one terrorist was killed and several suspects were taken into custody during a joint intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Bannu’s Miryan area, according to a press release issued by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD). The operation was conducted on the directives of KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed under the supervision of Bannu DPO Capt (retd) Mohammad Furqan Bilal in Khanni Kala, Barkazai and adjoining areas. The CTD said an exchange of fire took place between law-enforcement personnel and terrorists, resulting in the killing of an unidentified terrorist. The body was taken into custody and the identification process was initiated. “A Kalashnikov, three magazines and a bandolier were recovered from the slain terrorist”, it said. Several suspects were also detained during search and raid operations in the area, while further investigation was under way. The DPO praised the participating personnel for the successful operation and said IBOs would be intensified to make Bannu a peaceful place and eliminate terrorism and crime. He also urged residents to cooperate with law-enforcement agencies and immediately report any suspicious activity or persons to the police, according to the CTD. Bannu district has been the scene of repeated security incidents in recent months, with both civilians and local security forces coming under attack amid a broader surge in militant violence. This has prompted targeted counterterrorism operations by police and security forces. Last month, security forces killed 24 terrorists in Bannu district and its adjoining areas, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. Police later said another terrorist was killed as an operation continued for the third day. On July 23, security officials said the number of suspected militants killed during the operation had risen to 48 .

items.title: Affaire DZ Mafia : Gérald Darmanin remercie une nouvelle fois Alger
items.description: Deux membres importants de la DF Mafia ont été arrêtés ces derniers jours en Algérie. Recherchés en France pour leur implication présumée dans cette organisation mafieuse basée à Marseille, ils ont été placés sous mandat de dépôt en attendant leur jugement. L’occasion pour Gérald Darmanin , ministre de la Justice français, de remercier, une nouvelle fois, les autorités algériennes. « Les deux importants narcotrafiquants, objectifs prioritaires de la justice française, ont été placés en détention provisoire en Algérie à la demande du parquet d’Alger. Ils ne sont donc plus sous simple contrôle judiciaire », a annoncé Darmanin ce lundi 10 août sur son compte X. Le ministre de la Justice français en disant « merci aux autorités judiciaires algériennes pour nos échanges et pour notre collaboration au bénéfice de notre lutte commune contre le narcotrafic ». Le 5 août, Darmanin a annoncé une première arrestation en Algérie dans le cadre de la lutte en France contre la DZ Mafia. Il s’agit de Mehdi Laribi , considéré comme un membre fondateur et un chef au sein de l’organisation mafieuse française, et comme une « cible prioritaire de la justice française dans la lutte contre la drogue et la criminalité organisée », a précisé Gérald Darmanin. Le ministre de la Justice français n’a pas manqué de dire « merci aux autorités algériennes pour cette avancée et cette coopération en lien avec le parquet national anti-criminalité organisée (PNACO) et le parquet de Marseille ». Le lendemain, le même responsable a confirmé l’arrestation d’un autre cadre de DZ Mafia en Algérie. Il s'agit de Jamel Djeha, selon RTL. « Nouvelle preuve de notre efficacité dans la lutte contre la criminalité organisée : un nouveau cadre du narcotrafic et cible prioritaire de la justice française a été interpellé en Algérie par les autorités algériennes. Merci à elles pour cette coopération relancée au service de la sécurité de nos deux pays », a écrit Gérald Darmanin qui a effectué une visite en Algérie le 18 mai dernier. Ces arrestations marquent la reprise effective de la coopération sécuritaire et judiciaire entre l’Algérie et la France, après plusieurs mois de blocage total notamment en 2025 en raison des tensions entre les deux pays. Cette crise a éclaté en juillet 2024 à la suite de la décision du président Emmanuel Macron d’aligner la France sur les thèses marocaines concernant le Sahara occidental occupé. Puis, elle s’est aggravée avec l’arrivée de Bruno Retailleau au ministère de l’Intérieur la même année. Il aura fallu attendre une année après et la nomination de Laurent Nunez à Place Beauvau pour le début d’un dégel des relations entre les deux pays, mais les tensions persistent et Alger attend toujours des réponses de Paris notamment dans le dossier des biens mal acquis. items.title: Ashanti Region: Business owners, residents demand urgent action over bribery, extortion
items.description: Listeners who joined discussions on Luv FM in Kumasi shared experiences of alleged corruption across several sectors, including public institutions, revenue and regulatory agencies whose actions they say are crippling small businesses and undermining public trust. Their concerns come against the backdrop of the latest findings by the Ghana Statistical Service, which indicate that public officials solicited unofficial payments from nearly seven out of every ten people who encountered bribery situations during the second half of 2025. Small business operators who spoke during the discussions described what they called a culture of intimidation. According to them, some officials allegedly threaten to close down businesses and impose questionable tax assessments based on gross sales rather than profits. They also alleged that, in some cases, officials demand hefty bribes running into tens of thousands of cedis before offering relief or approvals. Many of the callers warned that such practices are discouraging entrepreneurship, shrinking already struggling businesses and deepening public mistrust in state institutions.

items.title: Mineurs marocains en Espagne : Ouahbi réclame une solution immédiate pour leur retour
items.description: Le ministre de la Justice, Abdellatif Ouahbi, a fermement appelé au retour au Maroc des enfants et mineurs marocains présents en Espagne, tenant la partie espagnole pour responsable de leur sort. Il a affirmé que le Maroc réclamera leur retour sur les plans juridique et politique. Dans une déclaration à Hespress, Ouahbi a indiqué que « le Maroc reste attaché à la récupération de ses enfants et de ses mineurs présents en Espagne, y compris ceux qui sont récemment entrés dans la ville de Sebta ou dans d’autres centres » , soulignant qu’il n’est nullement question de renoncer aux enfants et adolescents marocains. Le ministre de la Justice a affirmé que le Maroc « réclamera ses enfants sur les plans juridique et politique » , considérant que la responsabilité de la partie espagnole est engagée concernant le sort de ces mineurs et les conditions dans lesquelles ils vivent loin de leurs familles et de leur pays. Il a ajouté que la solidité des relations entre le Maroc et l’Espagne, ainsi que le niveau avancé de coopération et de coordination atteint entre les deux pays, exigent de trouver une solution immédiate à ce dossier, garantissant le retour des mineurs marocains auprès de leurs familles et dans leur pays, tout en préservant l’esprit de partenariat et les bonnes relations entre Rabat et Madrid. Le ministre a insisté sur le fait que le meilleur environnement pour garantir un avenir meilleur à ces enfants reste celui de leurs familles et de leur pays. Il a réaffirmé que « le Maroc n’est pas disposé à abandonner ses enfants, ses jeunes et ses adolescents » , précisant que cette position concerne l’ensemble des mineurs marocains concernés par ce dossier. Le responsable gouvernemental a renouvelé son affirmation selon laquelle Rabat réclame le retour de tous ses enfants et que le traitement de leur situation doit avant tout prendre en compte leur intérêt, leur avenir et leur droit à retrouver leur environnement familial. Cette prise de position intervient alors que le dossier des mineurs marocains avait déjà fait l’objet de consultations entre le ministre marocain de la Justice et son homologue espagnol. Ces discussions avaient porté sur les moyens juridiques et institutionnels de traiter la situation de ces enfants, ainsi que sur les mécanismes permettant de vérifier leur identité et de les réunir avec leurs familles. Ouahbi avait précédemment souligné que l’Espagne est, pour le Maroc, un pays ami et que la préservation des relations entre les deux pays demeure essentielle. Il avait estimé que la coopération juridique et institutionnelle ainsi que le dialogue direct constituent les moyens de résoudre les problématiques liées à la migration et aux mineurs. items.title: Only 59.3% of Ghanaian households have access to improved toilet facilities – Ministry of Local Government
items.description: Only 59.3% of households in Ghana have access to improved toilet facilities , highlighting persistent gaps in sanitation despite progress in other areas of water and sanitation delivery. The figure, cited by the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, means a significant proportion of households still lack access to improved sanitation facilities. The Ministry said the situation remains a concern, particularly in underserved communities where access to safe and dignified sanitation services continues to lag. The data forms part of the country’s broader Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) picture highlighted as Ghana marked the 2026 African Day for Decentralisation and Local Development on Monday, August 10. While 87.7% of Ghanaian households have access to basic drinking water services , sanitation outcomes remain a major challenge. The Ministry also pointed to inequalities in access to improved household toilet facilities, alongside challenges with wastewater management and sustainable solid waste disposal. “Addressing these challenges requires stronger local institutions, enhanced community participation and increased investments in sanitation infrastructure and services across the country,” the Ministry said. Government says Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies have a central role to play in addressing the sanitation deficit because they are responsible for planning and coordinating many essential services at the local level. The Ministry said it is therefore working to strengthen MMDAs through improved institutional capacity, sustainable financing arrangements and stronger partnerships with other stakeholders. These include Regional Coordinating Councils, Ghana Water Limited, the Community Water and Sanitation Agency, development partners, civil society organisations, traditional authorities and religious institutions. The Ministry also stressed the role of traditional and religious leaders in mobilising communities and promoting behavioural change around sanitation and environmental protection. The 2026 African Day for Decentralisation and Local Development was observed under the theme “Empowered Local Governments for Sustainable Water and Sanitation: Advancing Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Cities and Territories towards Agenda 2063.” The Ministry said improving sanitation is critical not only to public health but also to building resilient and sustainable communities. It called for stronger collaboration and increased investment to expand access to safe sanitation services, particularly among communities that remain underserved.

items.title: NERC sacks Kaduna DisCo’s board over N456bn debt, appoints interim administrator
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has dissolved the board of Kaduna Electricity Distribution Company (KAEDC) and appointed its Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Abubakar Umar Hashidu, as administrator for an initial six-month period, citing severe financial, operational and regulatory failures. The regulatory intervention, contained in Order No. NERC/2026/086, issued on Monday, took effect from August 10, 2026, and followed an inquiry and consultations with key industry stakeholders, including the Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE). According to NERC, KAEDC was in a “grave situation” characterised by prolonged regulatory and market default, inadequate investment, weak operational and commercial performance, insufficient assets relative to its liabilities and an inability to present a credible pathway to sustainable recovery. The Commission said the DisCo’s cumulative market obligations since privatisation stood at approximately N456.5 billion as of May 2026, comprising N415.5 billion owed to the Nigerian Bulk Electricity Trading Plc (NBET) and N41 billion owed to the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO). It added that KAEDC had accumulated another N14.26 billion in non-market statutory and third-party obligations. NERC further said that since ASI Engineering Limited (ASI) took over operations of KAEDC in June 2024, the DisCo had incurred an additional N118.6 billion in market debt as of May 2026. The Commission said ASI and KAEDC had “persistently failed” to furnish NBET and NISO with acceptable payment bank guarantees as required under their Vesting Contract and the Market Rules of the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI). The core investor also failed to provide a credible payment plan for the outstanding liabilities, NERC said. The Commission cited KAEDC’s poor remittance performance as another reason for the intervention. It said the DisCo paid only 41.93 per cent of adjusted market invoices in 2025, leaving a market shortfall of approximately N46.71 billion. The poor remittance performance was linked to KAEDC’s high Aggregate Technical, Commercial and Collection (ATC&C) losses, which stood at 71.88 per cent during the 2025 review period. “This means that in the 2025 review period, KAEDC was only able to account for only 28.2 per cent of the energy received and delivered to end-use customers,” the Commission said. NERC also faulted the investor’s capital expenditure performance, saying ASI failed to meet its capital injection commitments towards the recapitalisation of the utility. According to the order, KAEDC’s actual capital expenditure in 2025 was approximately N2.48 billion, against a minimum capital expenditure provision of N24.51 billion, representing only 10 per cent CAPEX performance. The Commission noted that the actual expenditure followed derogations and forbearances granted by NERC. The DisCo’s metering performance was also described as “abysmally low”, with meter coverage of its end-use customer population remaining between 33.26 per cent and 35.54 per cent since ASI took over the company, despite interventions aimed at supporting metering deployment. NERC said its earlier conditional no-objection of January 18, 2024 had approved the proposed acquisition of a 60 per cent equity stake in KAEDC by ASI, working with its nominated technical partner, Akanksha Power and Infrastructure Limited (APIL), subject to several conditions. These included evidence of APIL’s capacity to perform in Nigeria, a substantive technical-support proposal for KAEDC’s turnaround, a compliance plan for meeting NERC’s key performance indicators, a credible management team, a credible ATC&C loss-reduction trajectory and plans for bank guarantees in favour of NBET and the relevant market operator. However, NERC said ASI continued to fail to demonstrate full compliance with the requirements, while outstanding regulatory conditions remained unresolved. Against this background, the Commission dissolved the existing board and removed all its directors from office. It appointed an interim board chaired by Dr. Abdullahi Garba, with Engr. Francis U. Agoha, Mr. Aliyu E. Aliyu, Major General Henry E. Ayamasaowei (rtd), Dr. Haliru Dikko and Mr. Ayodeji A. Gbeleji, representing the BPE, as special directors. Hashidu was also appointed a special director for an initial six-month term and designated administrator of the DisCo. As administrator, he will oversee day-to-day operations, implement interim board resolutions and NERC directives, safeguard KAEDC’s assets and records, and handle matters reserved for approval by the Commission or interim board. NERC also withdrew the Key Yardstick Licence (KYL) approvals issued to members of KAEDC’s management team and directed affected staff to present themselves for revalidation. The Commission imposed restrictions on major financial and corporate decisions by KAEDC during the transition period, including borrowing, disposal or transfer of material assets, related-party transactions, changes to senior management remuneration, appointment or removal of senior officers and alteration of the company’s capital structure. The administrator was further directed to submit a costed 12-month stabilisation plan within 60 days, covering cash-flow controls, market remittances, collections, metering, energy accounting, loss reduction, service reliability, safety, customer complaints, capital expenditure, procurement, staff obligations and legacy liabilities. NERC said the special transition period would continue until the earlier of the completion of the transfer to a replacement core investor approved by the Commission, or termination, extension or variation of the intervention by a further order. The post NERC sacks Kaduna DisCo’s board over N456bn debt, appoints interim administrator appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Hypertension, acute asthma among conditions causing maternal deaths – Prof Sampene
items.description: Consultant forensic pathologist Professor Paul Ossei-Sampene has identified hypertension-related conditions and acute asthma among the conditions contributing to maternal deaths. His comments come amid rising maternal mortality in Ghana, with 965 maternal deaths recorded in 2025. Speaking on the JoyNews Desk on Monday, August 10, Prof. Ossei-Sampene said the reasons for maternal deaths were numerous and could be linked to several medical conditions affecting vital organs. “The reasons are quite numerous. Sometimes we attribute some of them to things like hypertensive-related conditions, which, of course, involve not only the heart but also some vital organs like the kidneys, heart and so forth. So basically, that is one,” he said. Prof. Ossei-Sampene cited a recent study published in 2025, which, according to him, indicated that hypertension-related conditions accounted for about 40.7 per cent of maternal deaths. “A recent study that was published sometime in 2025 said that hypertensive-related conditions that resulted in the death of mothers are around 40.7. So it means that the numbers are quite high,” he said. He added that, apart from hypertension, acute asthmatic conditions contribute to maternal deaths. Lack of education and harmful traditions Prof Ossei-Sampene also identified a lack of education among women as another concern, particularly where some women rely on customs and traditions that could be harmful to their health. He said some traditional beliefs and practices could be inimical to efforts to prevent maternal deaths. “Lack of education on the part of women who actually believe in customs and traditions which are actually inimical to some of these things that are actually causing maternal death is also a problem,” he said. According to him, misconceptions surrounding childbirth and changes to the female body were also influencing some women’s decisions about how they delivered their babies. He said some women believed that giving birth would cause them to lose some elasticity, a perception he said had led some to resort to various concoctions to reduce the size of parts of their bodies. “Now you realise that everybody, every woman, is actually … for the fact that a woman should use all manner of concoctions to reduce the size of whatever it is that they want to reduce.” Concerns over caesarean sections Prof Ossei-Sampene further raised concerns about women opting for caesarean sections because of fears about the effects of vaginal childbirth on their bodies. He referred to an instance in which the Deputy Minister of Health had visited a facility where a number of women had been lined up for caesarean sections despite, according to him, there being no indication for the procedures. He suggested that misconceptions about vaginal childbirth and concerns over possible changes to the vagina were among the factors influencing some women’s decisions. He also noted that men could sometimes contribute to such perceptions. “Sometimes, men also contribute to this. They may question why a woman should give birth naturally if it could result in the expansion of the vagina and other changes, which, of course, does not make any sense,” he said. Prof Ossei-Sampene said these concerns had led some women to choose what they considered to be the easiest method of delivery. “So most of the women also actually have decided that they will let them go for the easiest way possible, like removing the baby without any impact on the private parts like the vagina wall, ensuring that it’s exactly what it’s supposed to be,” he said. Risks associated with caesarean sections The forensic pathologist cautioned that caesarean sections could also be associated with complications. He explained that some complications following the procedure could include thrombosis and embolism. “Of course, when you do that, sometimes there are many minor things, and some of these minor things can [cause] thrombosis or embolism,” he said. According to Prof Ossei-Sampene, such complications could develop gradually and move through the system. “These can move gradually into the system. So, by the time the mother is ready to take the baby home, when she gets out of the bed and she collapses and dies,” he said. He stressed that such factors needed to be considered when examining the causes of maternal deaths. “So all these things are things that we need to actually, I mean, factor in,” he said. Prof Ossei-Sampene also expressed his support for efforts by the Deputy Minister of Health to address the challenges. “And I’m very glad that the Minister, the Deputy Minister, has actually taken up this challenge and [is] going to make sure that things are done properly, apart from the factors” he said.

items.title: Amazon founder Bezos nears deal to buy stake in Liverpool, reports say
items.description: A consortium that includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is close to agreeing a deal to acquire a ​stake of about one-third in Premier League club Liverpool, ‌multiple media outlets reported on Monday. The investor group also includes Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co-founder, according the reports. Sky News reported that ​the consortium is being led by Amit Bhatia, ​the son-in-law of steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal and a ⁠former shareholder in English second-tier club Queens Park Rangers, ​and that Liverpool owner Fenway Sports Group (FSG) could announce ​a deal as early as this week. The investment would reportedly value the club at approximately £4.4 billion ($5.9 billion), making it one of the largest ​valuations ever achieved in a football club deal. FSG, which ​acquired Liverpool in 2010, has explored outside investment in recent years ‌while ⁠retaining control of the club. A deal at the reported valuation would underline the substantial increase in Liverpool’s worth during FSG’s 16-year ownership. Neither Liverpool nor FSG immediately commented on ​the reports. Liverpool, who ​won the ⁠Premier League title in 2025, are entering a period of transition after the departure ​of manager Arne Slot and prolific forward Mohamed ​Salah. Michael ⁠Edwards, who was widely credited with helping build the squad that won Liverpool’s first English league title in 30 years ⁠in ​2020, left his role as chief ​executive officer of football at Fenway Sports Group in July.

items.title: Full list of African countries qualified for 2027 Women’s World Cup
items.description: The 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco is doubling as Africa’s qualifying tournament for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, with the four teams that reach the semi-finals earning automatic tickets to the global competition. Four countries have already secured their places at next year’s tournament in Brazil after advancing to the last four of WAFCON. They are Algeria, Morocco, Cameroon and Malawi, with each nation booking its place at the World Cup through its quarter-final victory. Meanwhile, Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa still have an opportunity to qualify through the play-off route. Here are the four African countries that have qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. 1. Algeria Algeria made history by securing their first-ever qualification for the FIFA Women’s World Cup after producing a remarkable comeback against Côte d’Ivoire. The Fennecs fell behind early but responded strongly to defeat the Ivorians 2-1 in their WAFCON quarter-final. Ines Khiri and Amira Ould Braham scored the goals that completed Algeria’s comeback and secured their place in the semi-finals. The victory means Algeria will make their debut at the FIFA Women’s World Cup in 2027. 2. Morocco Hosts Morocco also booked their place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup after overcoming South Africa 2-1 in the quarter-finals. Sakina Ouzraoui Diki and Hanane Ait El Haj were on target for the Atlas Lionesses as they progressed to the WAFCON semi-finals. The result keeps Morocco’s hopes of winning the continental title on home soil alive while also guaranteeing them a third successive appearance at the Women’s World Cup. 3. Cameroon Cameroon secured their World Cup ticket after stunning defending champions Nigeria in one of the biggest results of the WAFCON quarter-finals. The Indomitable Lionesses defeated the Super Falcons 1-0, with 19-year-old Myriam Nyadjou scoring the only goal of the encounter. Nyadjou’s long-range effort proved decisive as Cameroon advanced to the semi-finals and ended Nigeria’s hopes of retaining their African title. The result also guarantees Cameroon a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. 4. Malawi Malawi produced one of the biggest surprises of the tournament by defeating Ghana 2-1 to reach the WAFCON semi-finals and qualify for the World Cup for the first time. The Scorchers fell behind when Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah put Ghana ahead early in the match. Malawi responded through Temwa Chawinga, who restored parity before Rose Kadzere scored the winning goal. The historic victory secured Malawi’s first-ever qualification for the FIFA Women’s World Cup. WAFCON 2026 semi-final fixtures The four qualified teams will now battle for the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title. The semi-final matches are: Morocco vs Cameroon Algeria vs Malawi The winners will advance to the WAFCON final and compete for the continental championship. Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa still have a chance Although Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa were eliminated in the quarter-finals, their hopes of reaching the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup remain alive. The four teams will enter an additional African play-off, with the winners moving on to the intercontinental play-offs. Côte d’Ivoire will face Ghana on Thursday, while Nigeria will battle South Africa. The two winners will join the six other teams in the 10-team intercontinental play-offs, where three teams will ultimately qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. The tournament is scheduled to run from June 24 to July 25, 2027 , in Brazil. items.title: Sourou/Immersion patriotique obligatoire : Les appelés mettent en terre 210 plants
items.description: BURKINA-SOUROU-IPO-REBOISEMENT Sourou/Immersion patriotique obligatoire : Les appelés mettent en terre 210 plants Tougan, 10 août 2026 (AIB) – Les appelés de la deuxième édition de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) dans la province du Sourou ont mis en terre le dimanche 9 août 2026, 210 plants au sein du Complexe scolaire Notre-Dame de l’Annonciation (NDA) de Tougan, en présence du Haut-commissaire de la province, Désiré Badolo, et de plusieurs forces vives mobilisées pour accompagner l’initiative. Les appelés de la deuxième édition de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) dans la province du Sourou ont procédé, dimanche 9 août 2026, à une opération de reboisement au sein du Complexe scolaire Notre-Dame de l’Annonciation (NDA) de Tougan. Au total, 210 plants ont été mis en terre sur le site, dans le cadre des activités de formation civique et patriotique des appelés. L’activité s’est déroulée en présence du Haut-Commissaire de la province du Sourou, Désiré Badolo, président de la cellule provinciale de l’IPO, ainsi que de plusieurs forces vives de la province venues soutenir l’initiative. Selon le Haut-commissaire, cette opération de reboisement s’inscrit dans le chronogramme de formation des appelés de l’IPO 2026. « Dans le chronogramme de formation des appelés à l’IPO, cette journée de reboisement était inscrite. Cette activité de reforestation, visant à sauvegarder le couvert végétal, entre dans le cadre de la formation patriotique et civique des appelés », a-t-il expliqué. Le choix du site de NDA n’est pas fortuit, a précisé le Haut-commissaire. « Nous avons choisi le site de NDA parce qu’il est clôturé et offre davantage de garanties pour assurer un bon taux de survie des plants mis en terre. Les plants mis en terre sont également des espèces adaptées au sol », a-t-il ajouté. Désiré Badolo a invité les appelés à veiller à l’entretien et au suivi des plants afin de favoriser leur croissance et leur survie. Il a également rappelé que la première promotion des appelés de l’IPO dans la province avait réalisé une opération similaire sur le même site, avec un taux de réussite jugé satisfaisant. Agence d’information du Burkina SS/no/yos

items.title: La défense alerte sur la détérioration de la santé de Ghannouchi en prison
items.description: Le collectif de défense de l’ancien président de l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP), Rached Ghannouchi, a annoncé que son client, incarcéré depuis avril 2023, avait entamé une grève de la faim en prison et cessé de prendre ses médicaments depuis le jeudi 6 août 2026, pour protester contre son isolement total et la privation de ses droits, ultime recours pour les défendre. Dans un communiqué, le collectif a précisé que M. Ghannouchi, condamné à de lourdes peines de prison dans plusieurs procès intentés contre lui, avait été transféré à l’hôpital le 29 juillet dernier, ajoutant qu’il s’était vu interdire toute visite ou communication avec ses avocats et sa famille pendant 12 jours consécutifs, alors même qu’aucune information sur son état de santé n’était divulguée, malgré les demandes répétées adressées aux autorités compétentes. Le collectif de défense a fait porter aux autorités tunisiennes l’entière responsabilité des dépassements constatés ainsi que de toute complication susceptible de menacer la santé et la vie de son client, estimant que le traitement qui est infligé à l’ancien président du parti islamiste Ennahdha constitue une atteinte à son intégrité physique, d’autant plus qu’il est âgé de 85 ans et présente un état de santé fragile. Le collectif a également exigé que l’équipe d’avocats et la famille de Ghannouchi soient autorisées à lui rendre visite et à constater directement l’état réel de sa santé à l’hôpital. Le 5 février 2025, il est condamné à 22 ans de prison pour « conspiration contre la sûreté de l'État ». La peine est alourdie en appel en février 2026, ce qui porte la condamnation totale à plus de 40 ans de prison. I. B . items.title: KUMACA@70: Minister warns students against mob justice as REGSEC probes Obuasi SHTS unrest
items.description: The Ashanti Regional Security Council (REGSEC) has launched investigations into violent disturbances at Obuasi Senior High Technical School that occurred on Wednesday, August 5. Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, warned that anyone found culpable after the probe would face the full rigours of the law. The Headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, Abdullai Zakari, is currently on admission at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital after he was assaulted by rampaging students during a protest on campus. According to reports, the students vandalised school property and items at the headmaster’s bungalow. The protest was triggered by accusations that the headmaster had buried the body of a baby on school premises. Six students have been arrested by the police to assist with investigations into the disturbances. Addressing the 70th anniversary launch of Kumasi Academy, Dr. Amoakohene condemned the incident and said the Regional Security Council has taken over the matter to ensure accountability. “Just in the course of the week, we heard very terrible news from Obuasi SHTS where, for that matter, a headmaster was assaulted. Let me assure the general public that the state has taken a huge interest in the matter and wherever justice is due, same shall be served in due course,” he stated. Dr. Amoakohene used the opportunity to caution students across second cycle institutions in the region against taking the law into their own hands. He noted that while students have the right to raise concerns, destruction of property and assault cannot be justified under any circumstance. “Students gathered here, I am urging you: do not assault your teachers, do not vandalize school property even if you are in disagreement. Mob justice is one that our laws frown against. You have an SRC. In any event where there is disagreement, suspicion, or whatsoever, as future leaders who have been trained to replace us in the near future, you are encouraged to use the laid-down procedures in seeking justice and seeking redress as far as any issues are concerned,” he cautioned. He apologized to teachers on behalf of the students for acts of indiscipline on school campuses, and pledged that authorities and stakeholders would work hand in hand with teachers to address such incidents and prevent a recurrence. “So we want to say to our teachers that we are sorry. We are now ready to co-exist with you and work hand in hand with you,” the Minister said. Dr. Amoakohene was joined by other government officials who pledged the government’s continued support for infrastructure and academic development at the school. Kumasi Academy, established in 1957, has over the past seven decades produced thousands of graduates who are serving with distinction in both the public and private sectors across Ghana and beyond. The school has built a reputation for academic excellence, discipline, and leadership, and continues to be one of the leading second-cycle institutions in the Ashanti Region. Speaking at the event, the Chief of Nkwantakese, Nana Boakye Yam Ababio, who is also an old student of the school, charged the current students to live up to that legacy. He reminded them that Kumasi Academy’s name was built on hard work, respect, and order. “This school has trained many people who are currently working in various sectors. I am urging students that we will not accept any acts of violence or disturbances here. I have told them that protest should be the last resort in any disagreement with teachers. School property must not be destroyed. My advice to all students across Ghana is to stay away from such acts,” Nkwantakese Chief stated. He further urged the students to take their academics seriously, respect their teachers, and protect school property, noting that the progress of the school depends on the conduct of its students today. The leadership of the old students association pledged interventions that will improve teaching and learning in the school. The launch brought together members of the Ghana Baptist Convention, old students, teachers, management and students.

items.title: 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review deserves more scrutiny, it’s difficult to see the economic case – Dr Nsafoah
items.description: Dennis Nsafoah, an Assistant Professor of Economics at Niagara University in New York, has stated that Ghana’s 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review contains a policy choice that deserves much more scrutiny than it has received. According to him, while keeping the overall expenditure envelope broadly unchanged, the government has reallocated GH¢5 billion away from capital expenditure to GoldBod to fund the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP), whose objective is to raise international reserves to 15 months of import cover by 2028. In effect, Dr. Nsafoah, who is a member of the Research Committee of Tesah Capital, said the Mid-Year Review preserves total spending while shifting its composition from productive capital investment toward reserve accumulation. “That choice would already warrant debate on its own. But the recently released IMF [International Monetary Fund] staff reports make it considerably harder to defend. The IMF’s assessment is unusually clear: Ghana’s reserve adequacy is estimated at about six months of prospective imports, not 15. More importantly, the Fund explicitly states that reserves as high as the 15 months envisaged under GANRAP “would not be advisable on precautionary grounds alone” because of their non-negligible economic costs. Dr. Nsafoah argued that this begs the question: why is the government pursuing a reserve target that significantly exceeds what its principal multilateral adviser considers adequate while simultaneously reducing capital expenditure? “The IMF is not arguing against reserve accumulation. This distinction is important. The IMF is not recommending that Ghana stop building reserves. Its assessment is that Ghana, as a commodity exporter exposed to terms-of-trade shocks, capital-flow volatility and other external vulnerabilities, should maintain a healthy reserve buffer. Its estimate of adequate reserves is approximately six months of imports”. Fifteen Months has a Very Large Opportunity cost Dr. Nsafoah continued that the economics of reserve accumulation becomes less favourable as reserves rise, noting that at low levels, the benefits are substantial. He mentioned that reserves protect a country from sudden stops in capital flows, commodity-price shocks, temporary export disruptions and disorderly exchange-rate movements. However, those benefits diminish as the reserve stock becomes larger. He added that resources used to acquire low-yielding safe foreign assets could instead be deployed toward higher-return domestic investment. “This is no longer an abstract theoretical trade-off. The Mid-Year Budget has made it concrete. The government has directed GH¢5 billion to GoldBod for GANRAP while reducing capital expenditure by GH¢5 billion. In effect, Ghana is exchanging one form of national asset for another: fewer resources for productive capital formation today in order to accumulate a larger stock of foreign reserves”. He added that the relevant economic question is whether the return from moving Ghana’s reserves from an adequate level of around six months toward 15 months exceeds the return from roads, irrigation, energy infrastructure, hospitals, schools and other productivity-enhancing public investments. “It is difficult to see the economic case”, he added.

items.title: Burkina : Jean Jacques Kaboré décroche son doctorat avec une thèse sur la résistance des femmes à l’idéologie de la domination masculine au sein du foyer
items.description: BURKINA-SOUTENANCE-DOCTORAT Burkina : Jean Jacques Kaboré décroche son doctorat avec une thèse sur la résistance des femmes à l'idéologie de la domination masculine au sein du foyer Ouagadougou, 10 août. 2026 (AIB) -L'impétrant Jean Jacques Kaboré, de l'Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo de Ouagadougou, a brillamment soutenu, le lundi 27 juillet 2026, sa thèse de doctorat unique en Lettres, Langues et Arts, consacrée à la résistance des femmes face à l'idéologie de la domination masculine au sein du foyer dans certains pays africains anglophones. À l'issue de la soutenance, le jury lui a décerné la mention très honorable avec les félicitations du jury, le consacrant docteur en anglais. La soutenance s'est déroulée dans la salle de réunion des Écoles doctorales de l'Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo autour du thème : « Women's Resistance to the Patriarchal Ideology in some selected Anglophone African Plays », que l'on peut traduire par : « La résistance des femmes à l'idéologie patriarcale dans quelques pièces de théâtre africaines anglophones sélectionnées ». À travers cette recherche, le désormais docteur met en lumière les facteurs qui poussent certaines femmes à résister à la domination masculine, notamment les violences verbales et émotionnelles ainsi que les stéréotypes. Il analyse également les principales formes de cette résistance, parmi lesquelles la désobéissance et l'affirmation de soi, ainsi que leurs répercussions sur l'autorité masculine dans les sociétés africaines étudiées. Selon le Dr Jean Jacques Kaboré, l'objectif principal de cette étude était de proposer des pistes de réflexion susceptibles de favoriser une coexistence harmonieuse au sein des sociétés africaines. « Nous avons voulu mettre en lumière ces réalités dans certaines sociétés africaines afin d'apporter notre contribution à une vie harmonieuse. L'ultime solution pour une vie harmonieuse au sein des couples est que l'homme redéfinisse son comportement en tenant compte de la nouvelle identité de la femme qui est celle d'une femme qui lutte pour son émancipation», a-t-il déclaré. Après examen des résultats de la recherche, le jury a salué la qualité scientifique du travail tout en formulant quelques observations de fond et de forme qui seront prises en compte dans la version définitive de la thèse. Le jury international était présidé par la Pr F. Émilie Georgette Sanon/Ouattara, professeure titulaire à l'Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo. La direction de la thèse a été assurée par Alfred Kiema, maître de conférences à l'Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo, avec la codirection de Damlegue Laré, maître de conférences à l'Université de Lomé (Togo). Les rapporteurs étaient Aliou Sow, professeur titulaire à l'Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar (Sénégal), et Ayélé Fafavi d'Almeida, maître de conférences à l'Université de Lomé (Togo). Le jury comprenait également Fatou Ghislaine Sanou, maître de conférences à l'Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo, en qualité d'examinatrice. Au terme des délibérations, le jury a décerné à Jean Jacques Kaboré la mention très honorable avec les félicitations du jury. Agence d'information du Burkina SS/no/yos

items.title: Zoundwéogo: La police municipale et l’Association Zéro goutte de sang sensibilisent 16 888 usagers à la sécurité routière
items.description: Zoundwéogo: La police municipale et l’Association Zéro goutte de sang sensibilisent 16 888 usagers à la sécurité routière Manga, 7 août 2026 (AIB) – La police municipale de Manga, en collaboration avec l’Association Zéro goutte de sang, a sensibilisé 16 888 usagers de la route aux bonnes pratiques de circulation, au cours d’une campagne de sept jours, financée par l’Office national de la sécurité routière (ONASER). Menée du 31 juillet au 6 août 2026, la campagne avait pour objectif de sensibiliser les usagers de la route afin de contribuer à la réduction des accidents de la circulation dans la ville de Manga et ses environs, et d’améliorer les comportements routiers. Selon le directeur de la police municipale de Manga, le lieutenant de police Alidou Kéré, les actions de sensibilisation ont notamment porté sur le port du casque, l’utilisation du téléphone portable au volant ou au guidon, le port de la ceinture de sécurité, l’utilisation de sièges adaptés pour les enfants, le respect des feux tricolores ainsi que les règles d’arrêt et de stationnement. « Ces comportements sont accidentogènes et endeuillent de nombreuses familles chaque année. Pour les plus chanceux, ils s’en sortent avec des séquelles à vie », a-t-il souligné. Le bilan de la campagne fait état de 16 888 usagers sensibilisés, dont 9 302 hommes, 6 480 femmes et 1 106 enfants. Le responsable de l’Association Zéro goutte de sang, section de Manga, Florentin Ouédraogo, s’est dit satisfait des résultats obtenus. « Nous avons remarqué en une semaine un changement de comportement des usagers sur les routes », a-t-il déclaré. M. Ouédraogo a toutefois déploré la persistance de certains comportements indisciplinés et appelé à poursuivre la sensibilisation au sein des familles et dans les communautés afin d’ancrer durablement les bonnes pratiques en matière de sécurité routière. La police municipale et l’Association Zéro goutte de sang envisagent d’étendre leurs actions de sensibilisation aux établissements scolaires à la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027. Agence d’information du Burkina SM/BGB/bak

items.title: 2027: We must deliver Tinubu in Abia, Ikoh charges supporters
items.description: … Urges aggrieved APC members to back party’s candidates By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Former Minister and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship aspirant in Abia State, Chief Henry Ikoh, has urged his supporters to put the outcome of the party’s governorship primary behind them and mobilise for the victory of President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Ikoh, who is the Abia Coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors, spoke in Umuahia at the weekend while addressing supporters during a thank-you meeting organised to appreciate their backing during the governorship primary. He described the exercise as a “selection instead of election”, acknowledging the disappointment among his supporters following the emergence of Chief Eric Opah as the party’s governorship candidate. Despite the grievances, Ikoh urged his supporters to prioritise loyalty to the APC over personal ambitions, expressing confidence that the party would take over Abia in 2027. “My core mandate is to deliver Mr President and all APC candidates,” he said. He urged members of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors, Ozurumba Movement, Old Aba Division and other support groups to remain committed to the party. According to Ikoh, the APC must close ranks and strengthen its relationship with the Federal Government in order to attract more developmental benefits to Abia State. While acknowledging the economic challenges facing Nigerians, he expressed confidence in the reforms of the Tinubu administration, claiming that the naira had stabilised and states could no longer rely on borrowing to pay salaries. He appealed to Nigerians to remain patient with the administration, saying the reforms would eventually move the country from consumption to production. Reacting to claims that the Labour Party would win Abia in 2027, Ikoh dismissed such assertions as personal opinions. “That is their personal opinion. As a responsible APC man, you have to be APC all the way. “I am APC in the morning, afternoon and night. We must deliver APC in Abia,” he declared. The APC State Organising Secretary and Isuikwuato Local Government Coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors, Mr Emeka Okoroafor, commended Ikoh for remaining loyal to the party despite the controversy surrounding the governorship primary. Okoroafor claimed that 13 of the 18 members of the State Working Committee supported Ikoh during the primary, praising him for maintaining his position and choosing to mobilise support for the party. He, however, criticised what he described as alleged “double games” by some APC leaders who, according to him, were working against the party’s candidates. Also speaking, the State Coordinator of the Ozurumba Movement, Dr Paul Uzuegbu, pledged the group’s continued loyalty to the APC. “Our leader has spoken. Politics is about loyalty. We will follow his footsteps,” he said. The post 2027: We must deliver Tinubu in Abia, Ikoh charges supporters appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Patrick Vieira, un grand nom face au défi des Lions (Par Cheikh Gora DIOP)
items.description: Patrick Vieira n’a jamais vraiment eu besoin de présentation. Champion du monde en 1998, champion d’Europe en 2000, capitaine emblématique des Invincibles d’Arsenal, 107 sélections et 6 buts avec les Bleus : le joueur appartient au cercle des grandes figures du football français. Mais aujourd’hui, ce n’est pas le capitaine que la Fédération sénégalaise de football regarde. C’est l’entraîneur. Son nom circule parmi les prétendants susceptibles de succéder à Pape Thiaw sur le banc des Lions. À ce stade, il ne s’agit ni d’un choix arrêté ni d’une décision de la FSF. L’ancien milieu de terrain figure parmi les profils étudiés. Mais plusieurs sources confirment que Patrick Vieira tiendrait la corde parmi la pléthore de candidats. Une raison suffisante pour examiner son parcours avec objectivité, loin de l’emballement que peut susciter son immense carrière de joueur. Depuis sa reconversion, Vieira a dirigé cinq clubs en dix ans : New York City FC, l’OGC Nice, Crystal Palace, le Racing Strasbourg et le Genoa. Une expérience significative sur des bancs professionnels, mais une trajectoire faite de hauts et de bas, sans installation durable au sommet. À Crystal Palace, son début de mandat avait pourtant été prometteur. Pour sa première saison complète, il avait conduit les Eagles en demi-finale de la FA Cup. La dynamique s’est ensuite inversée avec onze matches sans victoire, entraînant son licenciement en mars 2023. À Strasbourg, son aventure s’est achevée à l’été 2024. Au Genoa, son arrivée avait permis de redresser une équipe menacée et de l’éloigner de la zone de relégation. Il avait même obtenu une prolongation avant que les résultats ne connaissent à nouveau un coup d’arrêt. Ces épisodes ne suffisent évidemment pas à juger son travail. Ils dessinent cependant le profil d’un technicien dont la trajectoire reste à confirmer au plus haut niveau et dont le bilan appelle davantage l’analyse que les certitudes. D’autant que le poste de sélectionneur présente des exigences très différentes de celles d’un entraîneur de club. Avec une sélection, les rassemblements sont courts et les séances limitées. Les joueurs arrivent de championnats et d’environnements différents. Il faut rapidement créer des automatismes, gérer les personnalités, installer une identité de jeu et préparer des compétitions où la marge d’erreur est réduite. À cela s’ajoutent les réalités propres au football africain. Sur ce terrain, Vieira part avec une particularité : il n’a jamais dirigé de sélection nationale. Il devra donc découvrir un exercice nouveau, avec ses contraintes et ses spécificités. Son expérience de joueur au plus haut niveau constitue toutefois un atout. Capitaine d’Arsenal et de l’équipe de France, il connaît la pression des grands rendez-vous et les exigences d’un vestiaire composé de joueurs de très haut niveau. Cette dimension peut compter dans la gestion d’un groupe sénégalais riche de plusieurs éléments évoluant dans les grands championnats européens. Son lien avec le Sénégal constitue une autre particularité. Né à Dakar le 23 juin 1976 avant de grandir en France, Vieira conserve des attaches concrètes avec son pays natal. Présent ces derniers jours dans la capitale, il partage son temps entre ses engagements professionnels et quelques moments de détente. Il s’est notamment rendu à Diambars, centre de formation dont il est l’un des membres fondateurs, aux côtés de Saër Seck, Jimmy Adjovi-Boco et Bernard Lama. Cette proximité avec le Sénégal est réelle, mais elle ne saurait se substituer aux critères sportifs dans le choix d’un sélectionneur. Selon certaines informations autour des discussions avec la FSF, Vieira n’aurait pas été initialement particulièrement attiré par l’idée de diriger une sélection, lui qui a privilégié jusque-là la carrière en club. Mais la perspective d’un projet de reconstruction à long terme à la tête des Lions, articulé autour de l’horizon 2030, aurait toutefois renforcé son intérêt pour cette possibilité. Reste que son nom n’est qu’un parmi plusieurs. Pat Vieira figure dans une réflexion qui inclut notamment Omar Daf et d’autres techniciens attirés par le prestige d’une sélection devenue l’une des références du continent. Finaliste de trois des quatre dernières CAN et double champion d’Afrique, le Sénégal dispose aujourd’hui d’un statut qui rend son banc particulièrement attractif. La question n’est donc pas de savoir si Vieira possède le prestige nécessaire, mais si son expérience, sa philosophie et sa capacité d’adaptation correspondent au projet que la Fédération veut construire. Son immense carrière de joueur ne constitue pas une garantie, pas plus que ses passages contrastés en club ne condamnent son profil. Vieira est un prétendant parmi d’autres, avec des atouts évidents et des inconnues à lever. En attendant le choix, très attendu, du futur sélectionneur, la FSF et sa tutelle devront d’abord accorder leurs violons sur les indemnités de départ de Pape Thiaw. Dans cet entre-deux, l’instance fédérale devrait confier provisoirement les Lions au Directeur technique national, Souleymane Diallo. Il pourrait ainsi conduire l’équipe lors des deux premières journées des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, face au Mozambique à Dakar, le 23 septembre, puis à l’Éthiopie à Addis-Abeba, le 27 septembre. cheikhgora.diop@lesoleil.sn

items.title: 457 Nigerians deported in 18 months as Germany emerges EU deportation hub
items.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom Germany has cemented its position as the leading deportation hub for Nigerian migrants in Europe, with no fewer than 457 Nigerians forcibly returned to Nigeria in the last 18 months through 14 chartered deportation flights hosted from German cities. Data compiled by the Deportees Emergency Reception and Support team, DERS, and obtained by Vanguard shows that between January 2025 and May 2026, German authorities coordinated or participated in every major monthly removal operation from Europe to Nigeria, with Lagos receiving over 80 percent of the returnees. According to DERS records, also shared by Refugees4Refugess.org, 171 persons — 143 of them directly from Germany — were deported onboard four charter flights in the first half of 2025. In the second half of the year, another 135 persons arrived in six separate interventions, except for the August flight, which DERS said was missed due to heavy rainfall. DERS noted that while at least two of these deportation operations were solely enforced by Germany with coordination by the state of Bavaria, the rest were carried out as a joint EU deportation operation with Vienna, Luxembourg, Italy, Cyprus, and Poland among others. Between January and May 2026, the pace did not slow down. DERS documented the deportation of 147 Nigerians in German-hosted joint EU charter operations, including a batch of 23 persons in May alone. A breakdown of the 2026 deportation figure shows that 27 persons were deported from Stuttgart in February. The operation, largely enforced by Baden-Württemberg, also included one severely ill person flown in from Slovakia. On March 10, 2026, 50 returnees landed in Lagos, including three women and six children in a joint EU operation hosted by Germany with Spain, Austria and Belgium. Germany accounted for 37 of those deported, a figure DERS described as the highest single enforcement in three years. Further breakdown shows that 24 persons, including two mothers and a 10-year-old minor with asthma, were flown in from Frankfurt on April 8, 2026, while another 23 were removed in May. DERS blamed the removals on mass denial of residence extensions by Berlin under Paragraph 104c. According to DERS, what has become very obvious is the ongoing deportation of many who, after the first 18 months, are denied extension of Paragraph 104c. “These strategic denials are usually attributed to claims that applicants did not meet required German integration benchmarks such as certified language courses, gainful employment and national identity documents,” the group said. DERS further alleged that the Paragraph 104c regularization scheme was “from the onset another reproduced deception to engage so-called Tolerated “Duldung” holders to actively cooperate in obtaining national identity documents as a criterion for extension.” The group said those passport documents were needed to facilitate Berlin’s massive deportation agenda. Human stories behind the statistics Beyond the numbers, DERS said the operations were leaving behind deep humanitarian scars. On March 10, a mother traveling with two children — one autistic and hyperactive — arrived in Lagos without preparation or resources. “Autism requires specialized support, patience, and routines, things that are difficult to maintain during forced travel,” DERS reported. Fellow returnees described the situation as “heartbreaking.” In February, a single mother with a valid residence permit and her three German-born children were deported from Sindelfingen, Stuttgart, after police allegedly ignored proof that they were due to collect residence cards. The family, who had lived in Germany for nine years, only returned to Germany after intervention by volunteers. Another mother deported in April lamented separation from her three children now in the care of the child welfare department in Paderborn, while the second mother who was deported from the Tuttlingen region was trapped in deportation despair with herself and her 10 years old daughter with an asthmatic condition. Moreso, one of the deported persons, according to DERS, reported he was residing in Spain but was arrested during his visit to Germany on March 15 in Kehl. He was detained for about three weeks and speedily processed for this deportation to Nigeria. The April German-wide\Frontex deportation operation was enforced onboard a World2Fly charter aircraft that departed Frankfurt in the early hours and arrived shortly before 1PM at the cargo airport in Lagos. Stuttgart as new hub DERS warned that Stuttgart and Baden-Württemberg are fast becoming the center of Germany’s deportation machinery. With the December 2025 and February 2026 operations both departing from Stuttgart, and with AFRICOM also located in the state, the group accused Germany of “positioning itself as the centre for colonial continuity in the so-called global south.” “The deliberate and repeated act of state violation of international legal provisions as well as Germany’s own domestic laws to enforce deportation is a cause for concern that we must continue to denounce,” DERS stated. DERS faults government’s silence The group also faulted the Nigerian government for what it described as a lack of reaction to years of reports of violence and rights abuses linked to the removals. “For the past two decades, Nigeria has always taken the top lead as the major deportation destination country for Germany,” DERS said, calling on the diaspora community to raise its voice against increasingly restrictive and inhuman migration policies. With monthly deportation routines still ongoing and more mobile identification hearings scheduled in Karlsruhe, DERS advised Nigerians with ‘Duldung’ tolerated status in Germany to take precautions. The removals have come at a huge cost to German taxpayers. DERS noted that the first half of 2025 operations alone were accompanied by 351 security personnel and gulped about €1.5 million. The figure, DERS said, does not cover costs for random police arrests, court conveyance, or deportation custody. The post 457 Nigerians deported in 18 months as Germany emerges EU deportation hub appeared first on Vanguard News .
